result.summary: Anthropic documents most of the pieces needed for an always-on operator as available on subscription logins: channels (push events into a running session), routines (cloud schedules and API-triggered runs), Remote Control, background sessions, /loop, and cloud-session follow-ups from the CLI. None of them is, as a whole, an explicitly permitted way to run an unattended company sales operator on a Pro or Max login. Channels are a research preview. The only officially approved channel plugins are Telegram, Discord, iMessage (macOS only) and a fakechat demo, so WhatsApp needs a custom channel. On Pro/Max a custom channel only runs through --dangerously-load-development-channels, which the docs describe for testing, which needs an interactive terminal, and which is ignored under -p and the Agent SDK. On Team/Enterprise an admin can allowlist an internal channel plugin, the cleaner supported route. Routines are the most clearly supported schedule and API-trigger option, but they run on Anthropic's cloud, have no mid-run approval step, and cannot reach a private VPS on Pro/Max. The consumer terms bar automated access unless explicitly permitted, and the Claude Code legal page says subscription OAuth is for ordinary use and points developers building products to API keys. Docs were checked live on 2026-10-14. The Anthropic docs map shows a last-updated stamp of 2026-10-14 03:39 UTC.

findings.topic: Channels: status, plans, auth requirements
findings.detail: Channels are a research preview. The docs say: 'They require Anthropic authentication through claude.ai or a Console API key, and are not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. Team and Enterprise organizations must explicitly enable them.' Pro and Max users without an organization opt in per session with --channels. Team and Enterprise need an Owner to enable channels (Organization settings > Claude Code > Channels) or set channelsEnabled in managed settings. The feature-availability matrix shows Channels available on Pro and Max, admin-enabled on Team and Enterprise, and available with a Console API key. Channels are therefore not subscription-only, unlike Routines and Remote Control. Events only arrive while the session is open. The official pages I read state no minimum version for channels. A third-party write-up cites v2.1.80, which I could not verify. Permission relay requires v2.1.234 or later.

findings.topic: Channels: official plugins and the WhatsApp gap
findings.detail: Officially included in the research preview: Telegram, Discord, iMessage (macOS only, reads chat.db and replies via AppleScript) and fakechat (a localhost demo). Each plugin requires Bun. There is no WhatsApp plugin. Telegram setup is /plugin install telegram@claude-plugins-official, then /telegram:configure <token>, then claude --channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official, then pairing and /telegram:access policy allowlist. I read the Telegram plugin source via WebFetch (summarized, not line-verified). It declares both claude/channel and claude/channel/permission. It exposes reply, react, download_attachment and edit_message tools. It relays permission prompts to allowlisted chats as Allow and Deny inline buttons. Its access state lives in ~/.claude/channels/telegram/access.json, with DM policies pairing, allowlist or disabled.

findings.topic: Custom channel build contract
findings.detail: A channel is an MCP server that Claude Code spawns as a subprocess and talks to over stdio, on the same machine. It must declare capabilities.experimental['claude/channel'] = {}. For a two-way channel it also declares tools: {} and a reply tool. It may declare capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission'] = {} for permission relay. It pushes events with mcp.notification({method: 'notifications/claude/channel', params: {content, meta}}). Meta keys must be letters, digits or underscores; others are silently dropped. Each event arrives as a <\channel source=...> tag. Only @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is required; Node, Deno or Bun all work. The reference's webhook example listens on 127.0.0.1:8788 with no authentication, so the Flask side needs its own shared secret. Claude Code does not acknowledge notifications. The await resolves when the message is written to the transport, not when Claude processes it. If the server is not loaded as a channel, events are dropped silently with no error returned. Events queue and are delivered together on the next turn when Claude is busy. Independent streams need separate sessions.

findings.topic: Getting a custom channel to run: Pro/Max vs Team/Enterprise
findings.detail: During the preview, --channels accepts only plugins on Anthropic's allowlist (claude-plugins-official) or on an org allowlist. A custom channel can run only with --dangerously-load-development-channels, in plugin:<name>@<marketplace> or server:<name> form. That flag shows a full-screen warning that must be accepted interactively. It is ignored with -p and the Agent SDK, so the channel does not register there. It does not bypass channelsEnabled, and it is per entry. The docs describe it for testing: 'To test a channel you're building, pass it to --dangerously-load-development-channels.' Community-marketplace plugins are not on the allowlist. On Team and Enterprise, an admin can set allowedChannelPlugins in managed settings with channelsEnabled true, naming their own marketplace plugin. Users then launch with --channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace> and no dev flag. That is the documented route for an internal custom channel. The docs do not say whether the dev-flag dialog reappears on every restart.

findings.topic: Permission relay to a phone or chat
findings.detail: A channel that declares claude/channel/permission receives notifications/claude/channel/permission_request with request_id (five lowercase letters, no 'l'), tool_name, description and input_preview. It replies with notifications/claude/channel/permission carrying request_id and behavior 'allow' or 'deny'. Relay covers tool-use approvals such as Bash, Write, Edit and MCP tool calls; the reference example relays mcp__webhook__reply. It does not cover project trust or MCP server consent dialogs. The local terminal dialog stays open, and whichever answer arrives first is applied. Only prompts that actually occur are relayed, so pre-allowed tools, auto mode and bypass mode skip it. Relay needs Claude Code v2.1.234 or later and the server opted in with --channels. The docs warn: 'Anyone who can reply through the channel can approve or deny tool use in your session.' The sender allowlist is therefore the security boundary.

findings.topic: Sender gating and prompt injection
findings.detail: Every approved channel keeps a sender allowlist. Only added sender IDs can push messages, and everyone else is silently dropped. The reference says to gate on the sender identity (message.from.id), not the room, because group membership would otherwise let anyone in an allowlisted group inject text. The docs say: 'An ungated channel is a prompt injection vector.' Customer WhatsApp text would enter Claude's context as event content and must be treated as untrusted input. A channel listens for events only when it is loaded via --channels, and a server must be named in --channels, not merely present in .mcp.json.

findings.topic: Telegram cannot be triggered by a server directly (inference)
findings.detail: Telegram's bot FAQ says bots will not see messages from other bots, regardless of privacy mode. A message the CRM posts through the Bot API is not an inbound update for the bot. My reading, not tested: the official Telegram channel only receives human-originated messages, so using it for server-originated WhatsApp events would require a human to forward each one. A custom channel is needed for server-originated events. This is a Telegram platform behavior I inferred from the FAQ, not an Anthropic statement.

findings.topic: Routines: triggers, API fire, and approval behavior
findings.detail: Routines are a research preview available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. They are created at claude.ai/code/routines or with /schedule, and /schedule needs a claude.ai login (not an API key or a cloud provider). Each run is a new Anthropic-cloud session that clones the chosen repositories. Triggers: schedule (minimum one hour), API, and GitHub events. The API trigger is a per-routine bearer token. POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/claude_code/routines/<id>/fire with header anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 and optional JSON body {text}. It returns a session URL. The docs say the endpoint 'is available to claude.ai users only and is not part of the Claude Platform API surface', and list internal tools and alerting systems as uses. Fire text is wrapped in an untrusted <routine-fire-payload> block, so the saved prompt must reference it. Runs do not pause for permission: 'Claude can use every tool from an included connector, including writes, without asking for permission during a run.' The docs also say the fired prompt 'is not live user input and can't act as approval or consent for actions during the run.' Local CLI MCP servers do not appear as routine connectors; they must be added as claude.ai connectors or committed in .mcp.json.

findings.topic: Routines: limits and usage
findings.detail: Scheduled runs: 100 per hour per account. Run now, API fires and one-off re-runs: 30 per hour per routine, one shared count. API fires: 100 per hour per account. None of the hourly limits has overage. Runs draw down subscription usage like interactive sessions. When the subscription limit is hit, runs continue on metered overage only if usage credits are on; otherwise they are rejected until the usage window resets. Each API fire starts a new session, so conversation memory does not carry across events. The docs do not state fire-to-start latency.

findings.topic: Reaching a VPS: self-hosting and network access
findings.detail: Routines and cloud sessions run on Anthropic-managed infrastructure unless an organization routes them to a self-hosted environment. Self-hosted environments are a public beta for Team and Enterprise only and are off by default. On Pro and Max, a routine cannot SSH into or reach a private VPS. Any VPS access must be a public HTTPS endpoint on a domain that is allowed in the environment's network settings. The default Trusted level permits only the default allowlist. Requests outside it fail with 403 host_not_allowed. Connector traffic goes through Anthropic and needs no allowlist entry. Cloud-environment network secrets (Pro and Max) store keys that are attached to matching outbound requests outside the sandbox, so the session never sees the raw value.

findings.topic: Cloud-session follow-ups from the CLI (documented event injection)
findings.detail: claude -p 'your message' --cloud <session-id> queues one message into an existing cloud session and exits. You can also pipe the message on stdin. It requires an Anthropic account sign-in (claude auth login), not an API key, and the org's allow_remote_sessions policy must be enabled. It is not available with a third-party provider. The docs name CI scripts as a use case. Cloud sessions are Anthropic-hosted and consume plan usage. When a session is idle, its VM is reclaimed ('Environment expired'). Reopening provisions a fresh VM and restores conversation history, but not background work or a self-paced /loop. Delivery latency and the behavior of --cloud after expiry are not documented.

findings.topic: Remote Control
findings.detail: Available on Pro and Max, and on Team and Enterprise once an Owner enables it. Requires a claude.ai full-scope login. The docs say 'API keys are not supported', and a setup-token token 'can't establish Remote Control sessions'. Server mode is claude remote-control, which asks 'Enable Remote Control? (y/n)' once. Run in a non-terminal context, an untrusted directory fails with a 'Workspace not trusted' error. Trust is never saved in the home directory. The local process must keep running, so the docs recommend tmux or screen on a server. The connection is outbound HTTPS only. Sessions reconnect after network drops. Server mode gives up after about 10 minutes of outage and exits. Permission prompts are forwarded to the web and phone and stay open until answered. Push notifications for 'actions required' can be enabled in /config. Trusted Devices (beta) requires a sign-in no older than 18 hours with biometric step-up. If an Owner or a Pro/Max user turns it on, unattended sessions break, so keep it off for the VPS identity. Remote Control is unavailable to ZDR and HIPAA organizations.

findings.topic: Background sessions (claude --bg, agent view)
findings.detail: claude --bg 'prompt' or claude agents starts a session that a supervisor process runs. The docs say 'Background sessions don't need any terminal open to keep working.' Shutting down or restarting the machine stops them. Sessions show as failed within 48 hours and as stopped after that. Sleep is fine. A finished or waiting session that stays unattached for about an hour has its process stopped, and its conversation resumes on the next reply. Permission prompts put the session in 'Needs input'. Peek replies do not answer dialogs: 'replying doesn't answer it', so you must attach. Background sessions consume subscription usage. An expired login appears as a blocked state. --bg cannot be combined with -p.

findings.topic: In-session /loop and cron scheduling
findings.detail: Tasks are session-scoped. They fire only while Claude Code is running and idle, and they do not catch up on missed fires. Recurring tasks expire after 7 days. A session can hold up to 50 tasks. On resume, tasks are restored except expired recurring ones and self-paced /loop tasks. Recurring tasks run late by up to 30 minutes, but */5 * * * * is not delayed. Backgrounding a session carries /loop tasks into a background session. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 turns the scheduler off.

findings.topic: Unattended permissions, auto mode, bypass and sandbox
findings.detail: Modes: default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions. Deny rules block in every mode, including bypass. Allow rules have no effect in bypass. Auto mode uses a classifier. In interactive sessions, 3 blocks in a row or 20 in total pauses auto mode and resumes prompting. In a -p run without --permission-prompt-tool, the blocked action simply does not run, and Claude keeps working. --permission-prompts none (v2.1.259+) denies anything that would prompt unless a PermissionRequest hook allows it. dontAsk denies anything not pre-approved. --dangerously-skip-permissions is documented for a container, VM or sandbox runtime, run as a non-root user on Linux or macOS. Actions no mode auto-approves include ask rules, AskUserQuestion, rm on critical paths, and the cross-session messaging safeguards. The Bash sandbox is built in on macOS, Linux and WSL2, and sandboxed commands get no network by default. Auto mode's default block list includes launching an autonomous loop without approval or a sandbox, such as one started with --dangerously-skip-permissions, and including sensitive details such as emails or account IDs in content sent to other people unless the user named them.

findings.topic: Hooks as a fail-closed approval backstop
findings.detail: A PermissionRequest hook can allow or deny on the user's behalf through hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior ('allow', optionally with updatedInput, or 'deny'). Exit code 2 is not honored for PermissionRequest, so denial must go through the decision object. With onFailure: 'block' (v2.1.295+), a failing or missing hook denies the request. HTTP hooks POST the hook input as JSON. A 2xx JSON body is parsed with the same schema. A non-2xx status or connection failure is non-blocking. Timed-out command and HTTP hooks are canceled, and the docs warn 'don't count on a stalled hook to act as a gate'. The docs recommend permission rules, not hooks, for hard allow and deny. Under -p with --permission-prompts none, a PermissionRequest hook is the only way to allow a request.

findings.topic: Auth traps: API key precedence and token types
findings.detail: Precedence: cloud-provider variables, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, profiles, then /login. The docs say: 'If you have an active Claude subscription but also have ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set in your environment, Claude Code uses the API key once you approve it.' They also say: 'In non-interactive mode (-p), the key is always used when present.' A stray API key on the VPS can therefore bill per token silently. claude setup-token creates a one-year token for CI and scripts. It requires Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise, can only make model requests, and cannot run Remote Control or fetch connectors. --bare ignores OAuth and the keychain, and Anthropic says --bare 'will become the default for -p in a future release', which would break subscription scripts that do not pass credentials. Logins warn three days before expiry. After expiry and failed refresh, requests fail until /login is run again, and the docs warn that unattended sessions stop progressing.

findings.topic: Context, compaction and restart behavior
findings.detail: Compaction is automatic. After compaction, the project-root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules are re-read from disk, up to five recently touched files are re-read, skill bodies are re-injected but truncated, and the conversation becomes a structured summary. SessionStart hooks matching the compact source re-run and add their output. Path-scoped rules can be summarized away. Sessions resume with --continue or --resume. Channel events only arrive while the session is open, so events sent during downtime should be assumed lost (inference from the docs, untested). State must therefore live in the CRM.

findings.topic: Subscription usage and billing exposure
findings.detail: Pro and Max include usage. Team and Enterprise seats have a rolling 5-hour window and a weekly window, shared with chat and Cowork. Routines, cloud sessions, background sessions and /loop all draw on the same usage. The docs give no absolute numbers for Pro or Max limits, so 24/7 capacity cannot be estimated from them. Measure with /usage, whose Loops rows show scheduled-task consumption. The legal page says advertised Pro and Max limits 'assume ordinary, individual usage'. Usage credits (metered overage) are off by default and can be enabled from /usage-credits. Keeping them off prevents per-token charges, but runs are rejected until the window resets.

findings.topic: Legal position: supported, gray, prohibited
findings.detail: (a) Documented for subscription plans: Channels (official), Routines including the API trigger, Remote Control, cloud-session follow-ups from CI scripts, setup-token for 'CI pipelines and scripts', /loop and background sessions. These are documented features. Nothing in the docs says they are permitted for unattended business operations. (b) Gray: Consumer Terms (Free, Pro, Max) section 3, item 7 says: 'Except when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it, to access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise.' The Claude Code legal page says: 'OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code.' It adds: 'Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice.' It directs authentication questions to sales. The Commercial Terms text I extracted (effective June 17, 2025) has no automated-access clause. The legal page applies the same OAuth ordinary-use language to Team and Enterprise. (c) Prohibited or disfavored: 'Developers building products or services ... should use API key authentication.' 'Anthropic does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users.' 'Developers may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens.' 'Customers may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf.' The counter-quote: 'Nor does it prevent an end user from signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription.' Classification: an internal company's use of the unmodified binary on its own subscription is closest to that counter-quote. Unattended multi-user business automation at volume is not addressed. If the system is offered to clients or partners, the prohibited category applies. This classification is my analysis, not an Anthropic ruling.

setup_steps: Legal and plan gate first: get a written answer from Anthropic sales on this exact architecture (the legal page directs authentication questions to sales). Decide between Pro/Max (individual plan, development-flag path, testing-grade) and Team/Enterprise (admin-allowlisted plugin path, cleaner but seat-priced). Keep usage credits off (claude.ai/settings/usage) so exhausted limits reject runs instead of billing per token.

VPS prep: create a non-root service user for the agent (the docs require non-root for --dangerously-skip-permissions and it is safer generally). Install Claude Code, update it to a current build (claude update), install tmux, and install Bun if you want the official plugins. Keep the Bash sandbox enabled. Run claude doctor.

Auth hygiene: in the service user's environment make sure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and apiKeyHelper are unset, because they outrank /login and -p always uses an API key when present. Run claude, then /login with the claude.ai account. Confirm the Login row in /status shows the subscription. Put a reminder before the 3-day login expiry warning to re-run /login.

Pre-trust the project directory interactively once, so trust is saved. Non-terminal starts of remote-control fail with 'Workspace not trusted'. Do not use the home directory, where trust is never saved.

Team/Enterprise only: an Owner enables Channels at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code. Then set managed settings channelsEnabled: true and allowedChannelPlugins listing your internal marketplace plugin, for example { marketplace: 'acme-internal', plugin: 'whatsapp-bridge' }. Pro/Max users skip this and use the development flag in step 9.

Build the WhatsApp channel server per the channels reference, using Node or Bun with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Declare experimental 'claude/channel' and 'claude/channel/permission' ({} each) and tools: {}. Add a reply tool. Write an instructions string that explains the <\channel source='whatsapp'> tag and says to reply with the reply tool using the chat_id attribute. Listen on 127.0.0.1 only. Require a shared-secret header that only Flask knows, and deduplicate by WhatsApp message ID. Emit notifications/claude/channel with content = message text and meta keys with letters, digits or underscores only (chat_id, msg_id, lead_id).

Gating: accept inbound events only from Flask (shared secret). Accept permission verdicts only from the owner's WhatsApp sender ID and ignore groups. Parse verdicts with the documented regex /^\s*(y|yes|n|no)\s+([a-km-z]{5})\s*$/i and lowercase the ID before emitting the verdict.

Permission relay: implement the notifications/claude/channel/permission_request handler. Send the owner the tool_name, description, input_preview and the line 'Reply yes <id> or no <id>'. Emit notifications/claude/channel/permission with request_id and behavior allow or deny. Test with curl before connecting WhatsApp, following the reference's webhook example.

Register the server in the project's .mcp.json. Expose CRM operations as a separate MCP server or as allowlisted commands. Permissions: add allow rules for read-only lead lookups. Leave send and update tools without allow rules so they prompt and get relayed. Add deny rules for destructive operations. Keep sandboxing on and set sandbox network allowlists for the CRM host.

Start the session in tmux: tmux new -s sales, then either claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:whatsapp (Pro/Max, testing-grade) or claude --channels plugin:whatsapp-bridge@acme-internal (Team/Enterprise). Accept the one-time dialogs, then detach with Ctrl-b d.

Keep-alive (my suggestion, not from the docs): a systemd unit for the service user that starts tmux and claude on boot and restarts it on failure. Test a reboot before relying on it, because the development-channel dialog or other prompts may block recovery. Add a heartbeat from the channel to Flask and alert the owner through a separate path if the heartbeat stops.

Memory: keep operating rules and the approval policy in project CLAUDE.md. Put lead workflows in skills. Add a SessionStart hook with a compact matcher that re-injects the current queue state from the CRM after compaction. The CRM is the system of record, not the context window.
Safety net for dropped events: a /loop 5m or CronCreate task that polls the CRM for unprocessed inbound messages and deduplicates by msg_id. Recreate it before the 7-day expiry.

Enforce approval in the CRM, not only in Claude: the send endpoint refuses any outbound message that lacks an owner-approval record, whatever the agent requests. This is the one control that does not depend on the agent or the terms.

Test plan before any production use: (a) measure end-to-end latency from curl POST to Claude's reply; (b) restart the session and check which events were lost; (c) send ten events while Claude is busy and check batching; (d) run an approval round-trip from the phone; (e) confirm zero API charges in the Console and that /usage shows only subscription usage; (f) run one week and watch the usage windows.

Alternative without a persistent session (Routines): create a routine at claude.ai/code/routines with an API trigger and store the per-routine token in Flask's secret store. POST to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/claude_code/routines/<id>/fire with the bearer token, the anthropic-beta header and {text: ...}. Reference the routine-fire-payload block in the saved prompt. Add the CRM HTTPS domain to the environment's allowed domains. Attach only the needed connectors. The routine proposes a reply, and the CRM sends only after owner approval.

Alternative for owner supervision: run claude remote-control in tmux on the VPS and approve prompts from the Claude app with push notifications. This needs no custom code, but it is human-driven and not event-driven. Inbound events still need the channel or Routines path.
limits_and_risks: Research preview: the --channels flag syntax, the protocol contract and the development-flag behavior may change. Routines' fire endpoint is also marked experimental, with its beta header versioned.

WhatsApp inbound needs a custom channel. On Pro/Max that means the development flag, which the docs describe for testing, requires an interactive terminal, and is ignored under -p and the Agent SDK. It does not bypass channelsEnabled.
Restarts need a human: the development-channel dialog, the Remote Control enable prompt and the workspace trust prompt all block headless restarts. Background sessions stop on machine reboot.
Silent event loss: channel notifications are not acknowledged, and if the server is not loaded, events are dropped with no error to the sender. Events during downtime should be assumed lost.

Routines have no mid-run approval. Connector writes run without asking, and each fire starts a fresh session with no conversation memory. Fires are capped at 30 per hour per routine and 100 per hour per account.
Routines cannot reach a private VPS on Pro/Max. Self-hosted runners are Team and Enterprise public beta only, so a VPS must be a public HTTPS endpoint on an allowlisted domain.

Approval gating is only as strong as the channel's sender gate. The docs say anyone who can reply through the channel can approve tool use. Customer message text is untrusted input and can carry prompt injection into the session.
In -p mode, a blocked auto-mode action is silently skipped and the run continues. Under interactive auto mode, three consecutive blocks or 20 total pause auto mode and resume prompting.

Background sessions cannot answer permission prompts from peek. The prompt needs an attached terminal, so unattended approvals must be pre-allowed, auto-classified, hook-decided, or relayed through a channel or Remote Control.
Stray ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper on the VPS silently switches usage to per-token API billing, and -p always uses the key when present.
Login expiry: unattended Remote Control and background sessions stop when the login expires and cannot recover until /login is re-run. setup-token cannot run Remote Control.

Usage windows: 24/7 operation will hit subscription windows. No absolute Pro/Max numbers are published in the docs. With usage credits off, runs are rejected until reset. With them on, overage is metered per token.
Trusted Devices (beta) requires sign-in within 18 hours with biometric step-up. If enabled for the org or on Pro/Max, unattended Remote Control breaks until a human re-authenticates.
Compaction keeps CLAUDE.md, up to five recently touched files and a summary, but loses detail. Path-scoped rules may be summarized away. Durable state must live in the CRM.

Idle background sessions have their process stopped after about an hour unattached and resume only on reply. /loop expires after 7 days, runs only when idle, and is limited to 50 tasks per session. Self-paced /loop does not restore on resume.

Terms risk: unattended business automation on a Pro/Max login is not explicitly permitted anywhere I found. Consumer Terms section 3(7) bars automated access except via API key or where explicitly permitted. Anthropic may enforce 'without prior notice'.

Default-behavior risk: the headless docs say --bare 'will become the default for -p in a future release'. Subscription scripts that do not pass credentials explicitly would then break. Reporting gaps to Anthropic: use /feedback.
result.verdict: Partly viable, not yet a clean always-on operator on a subscription. It is viable as a supervised pilot, not as an unattended production operator on a Pro or Max login. What breaks: (1) the WhatsApp inbound path is a custom channel. On Pro/Max it needs the development flag, which is testing-framed and interactive. On Team/Enterprise it needs an admin allowlist, which is cleaner but still research preview. (2) Restarts after a reboot need a human unless the setup is hardened, and background sessions die on reboot. (3) Events are not acknowledged and are dropped silently when the channel is not loaded. (4) Routines are the best-documented subscription feature for schedules and API triggers, but they have no mid-run approval, cannot reach a Pro/Max VPS, and start a fresh session per event. (5) Usage windows will throttle continuous work, and no absolute limits are published. (6) The terms do not explicitly permit unattended business automation on a Pro/Max login. Consumer Terms section 3(7) restricts automated access unless explicitly permitted, and the Claude Code legal page routes product-building developers to API keys. Before production, get written confirmation from Anthropic sales. Regardless of the platform chosen, enforce owner approval in the CRM rather than relying on the agent or the relay alone. The lowest-dependency supported path is Routines for bounded jobs with CRM-side approvals. Treat the persistent channel operator as a research-preview pilot.
open_questions: Does the development-channel warning dialog reappear on every start? This decides whether a reboot can recover unattended on Pro/Max. Test on the VPS.

Does claude -p with --channels, or a backgrounded session, stay alive to receive channel events? The docs say channels work with -p but do not say whether the process waits for events. Also, is --bg compatible with --channels?
Routines: what is the fire-to-start latency, and what subscription usage does each fire consume in practice? The docs give neither.
Cloud follow-ups: what is delivery latency with claude -p --cloud, and does a message to an environment-expired session resume it or fail?

Will Anthropic confirm in writing that an internal, unattended, multi-user sales agent on Pro/Max (or on Team) is 'ordinary use' or 'explicitly permitted'? The legal page says to contact sales for authentication questions.

Does the Team plan change the automated-access analysis? The Commercial Terms text I extracted has no automated-access clause, but the Claude Code legal page applies the same OAuth ordinary-use wording to Team and Enterprise. Confirm the governing terms for Team seats.
What are the actual Pro/Max and Team usage budgets for continuous runs? The docs publish mechanics but no numbers, so measure with /usage.
Can a PermissionRequest HTTP hook hold the request while waiting for the owner's reply (long-poll) within the hook timeout, and how does it race with relay? Test before depending on it.
Do MCP tool calls such as send_whatsapp get relayed to the channel's permission prompts in production? The reference example suggests yes, but I did not test it.
Telegram: does a server-originated Bot API message to a private chat ever produce an inbound update to the same bot? The FAQ suggests no. Verify before ruling the Telegram route in or out.
Which channel server behaviors does Anthropic's allowlist review require for an official listing? Partner coordination is mentioned, but the criteria are not published.

result.summary: Routines (claude.ai cloud, research preview) are the only officially documented way to run Claude Code unattended on a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise subscription with a schedule and an HTTP trigger. Schedule triggers have a 1-hour minimum and can start several minutes late. The per-routine /fire endpoint takes a bearer token and is capped at 30 fires per hour per routine and 100 per account. Runs execute in Anthropic's cloud sandbox, not on your VPS. Pro and Max routines have no documented shell or SSH access to your VPS, no approval prompts, and each fire starts a fresh session with no memory of earlier WhatsApp messages, so the CRM must hold all state. The only documented way to run on your own VPS with your own network and secrets is a self-hosted environment, which is public beta and limited to Team and Enterprise (Linux or macOS runner, Owner must enable it). On the legal side, routines are offered as a product feature on subscription plans, but Consumer Terms s.3 bars automated access except via API key or where Anthropic explicitly permits it, and the Claude Code legal page says OAuth is for ordinary use and that developers building products should use API keys. I found no official statement that always-on internal business automation on subscription auth is covered. DIY VPS scripts using account login or setup-token are gray. Offering this to other companies on subscription auth is prohibited. Everything below was verified against official pages fetched 2026-10-14 unless marked otherwise.

findings.topic: Routines: what they are, plans, where to create them
findings.detail: A routine is a saved Claude Code configuration (prompt, one or more GitHub repos, connectors, triggers). It runs as a cloud session on Anthropic-managed infrastructure by default, or on your org's self-hosted environment when routed there. Available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. Team/Enterprise Owners can switch routines off for everyone at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code. Still a research preview: 'Behavior, limits, and the API surface may change.' Create at claude.ai/code/routines, in the Desktop app (Code tab > Routines > New routine > Cloud), or via /schedule in the CLI (CLI requires claude.ai login, not an API key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry or a Console key). Each run is a new session that clones the repo(s) fresh, runs without a permission-mode picker or approval prompts, and counts against the owner's account. Routines belong to one individual account, not to a team, and actions appear as that person.

findings.topic: Schedule trigger: frequency, minimum interval, timezone
findings.detail: Presets: hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, or a one-off timestamp (one-off auto-disables after firing). Custom cron is set only from the CLI via /schedule update after picking the closest preset in the web form. Minimum interval is one hour; more frequent cron expressions are rejected. A run scheduled exactly on the hour (e.g. 9:00) can start several minutes late; the docs suggest an off-hour minute such as 9:07. Times are entered in your local zone and converted automatically, so for 06:00 IST use Asia/Kolkata and pick 06:07 (06:07 IST = 00:37 UTC). Comparison: Desktop scheduled tasks and /loop have a 1-minute minimum, but they run locally.

findings.topic: API trigger (/fire): endpoint, auth, headers, body, response, errors
findings.detail: Endpoint: POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/claude_code/routines/{trig_...}/fire. Auth: Authorization Bearer with a per-routine token (prefix sk-ant-oat01-), created only in the claude.ai web UI (Edit > Add another trigger > API > Generate token). The token is shown once; generating a new one revokes the old; the CLI cannot create, regenerate or delete tokens. The token is scoped to that one routine and gives no read access. Headers: anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 is the only accepted value and is required. The routines page shows anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 in its curl example and warns that breaking changes ship behind new dated beta headers; the API reference says the endpoint accepts requests with and without that beta header. The two pages disagree, so send both. Body: optional JSON {"text": plain string, max 65,536 characters}. The text is not parsed (JSON arrives as a literal string) and is wrapped in a routine-fire-payload block labelled as untrusted data, so the routine prompt must explicitly tell Claude to act on it. Success (200) returns {type: routine_fire, claude_code_session_id, claude_code_session_url} as soon as the session is created; it does not wait for the run. Errors: 400 (bad anthropic-version, text too long, or routine paused), 401 (token mismatch), 403, 404, 429 (hourly limit; Retry-After header), 500 (retry with backoff), 503 (retry after delay). There is no idempotency key: every successful call creates a new session, so caller retries duplicate runs. The endpoint is for claude.ai plan accounts only, not API keys, and is not in the Anthropic SDKs.

findings.topic: Run environment: what a cloud routine can reach
findings.detail: Each run is a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM (approx. 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 30 GB disk) with the repo cloned in and a setup script (cached only if it finishes in about 5 minutes). Network access per environment is None, Trusted, Full or Custom. The Default environment is Trusted, which allows package registries, GitHub and cloud SDKs only, so your CRM domain must be added (Custom, or Full). Connector traffic goes through Anthropic's servers and needs no allowlist entry. Sessions sit behind an HTTP/HTTPS proxy; I found no documentation of raw TCP or SSH from cloud sessions to a VPS, so treat SSH as unsupported unless you test it. Secrets: environment variables are readable by everyone who uses that environment. On Pro and Max only, 'network secrets' attach a key to requests for listed hosts so the session never sees it; Team and Enterprise do not have this yet and must use env vars. No documented maximum run duration or routine concurrency cap was found. Commands default to a 2-minute timeout (up to 10); idle VMs pause and can be reclaimed.

findings.topic: Self-hosted environment: the only documented way to run on your own VPS
findings.detail: Public beta, Team and Enterprise only, off by default. An Owner turns on 'Allow self-hosted environments' at claude.ai/admin-settings/cloud-environments. Pro and Max cannot use it. Runner: Claude Code v2.1.224 or later on Linux or macOS (Windows is not supported as a runner host). Command: claude self-hosted-runner --environment-secret-file <file> --base-dir <dir>. Guided setup: claude self-hosted-runner setup (needs an Owner sign-in). The environment key is shown once and expires 365 days after creation. The runner makes only outbound HTTPS to api.anthropic.com, and nothing connects inbound. Each session is a child Claude Code process on your host, cloning the repo with host git credentials. Shell commands, hooks and stdio MCP servers inherit the session environment and can read credential variables and files on the host, so use a dedicated low-privilege user, default-deny egress and no host secrets in the environment. Routines can be routed to it. Sessions on self-hosted environments consume the organization's Claude Code usage the same way cloud sessions do. Model inference goes to the Anthropic API using a session-scoped token issued by the control plane, not your own key. Limits: unavailable to orgs with Zero Data Retention or HIPAA; an org IP allowlist breaks Anthropic-hosted sessions but not self-hosted ones; any org member can dispatch sessions to the environment.

findings.topic: Permission model and how to restrict tools
findings.detail: No approval prompts for routine runs. Connectors that are included can use every tool, including writes, without asking. Routine artifact publishing asks first only in some cases. Cloud sessions pre-approve file edits, offer Accept edits, Plan and Auto modes (Auto only when the org allows it), and do not offer bypass permissions. Ways to restrict a routine: remove connectors per routine (all are included by default); choose a tighter network level; commit .claude/settings.json with permissions.deny (honored only in single-repo sessions); server-managed settings reach cloud sessions for Team/Enterprise; GitHub branch protection or rulesets limit which branches a push can update (the proxy does not). On self-hosted runners, routine tool calls including Bash are pre-approved by default, so the network boundary is what limits where they can reach.

findings.topic: Run limits and quotas (hourly caps and subscription usage)
findings.detail: Hourly caps: scheduled runs (including one-offs) 100 per hour per account; the run waits until the limit resets. Run now, API fires and re-arming a one-off share 30 per hour per routine. Run now and re-arming a one-off also count against 100 per hour per account. API fires have their own 100 per hour per account. Over the API limit the call returns 429 with Retry-After (no queue); over the Run now limit the action fails. None of these has overage. GitHub events have per-routine and per-account hourly caps that are not specified. Subscription usage: routines draw from the same usage pool as interactive Claude Code. The help article says Pro and Max have a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit shared across Claude and Claude Code; I did not find published exact figures. If usage credits are enabled, runs past the limit continue on metered overage; if not, they are rejected until the window resets. A paused subscription puts routines on hold. A third-party guide claims daily caps of 5, 15 and 25 runs; that claim is not in the official docs, so do not rely on it. Check usage with /usage in the CLI or at claude.ai/settings/usage.

findings.topic: Run history, failures, retries, notifications, GitHub dependency
findings.detail: Run list is on the routine's page at claude.ai/code/routines. A green status only means the session started and exited without an infrastructure error; it does not mean the task succeeded, so read the transcript. CLI: /schedule list, /schedule run, and asking why a run did nothing (v2.1.227+). RemoteTrigger actions list_runs and get_run_log also expose logs (in-session only). I found no routine-level email or push notification setting; desktop notifications apply only to local Desktop tasks, so owner alerts must come from a connector called in the prompt (for example Slack) or from your own CRM/Flask side. No automatic retry of failed sessions is documented. API callers must handle 429 and 5xx themselves, and duplicates are possible. If the GitHub connection is missing when a run is due, scheduled runs are skipped for up to 72 hours, after which the routine turns off until GitHub is reconnected.

findings.topic: RemoteTrigger tool: is it the programmatic interface to routines?
findings.detail: RemoteTrigger is an in-session Claude tool, not an external REST API. It backs /schedule. Actions: list, get, create, update, run, create_webhook_trigger, list_runs, get_run_log. body is required for create, update and create_webhook_trigger. It exists only in sessions signed in with a claude.ai account on a plan with routines enabled; it is absent when cloud sessions are disabled or, from v2.1.227, when routines are turned off by an Owner; it is not available on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry. The only documented external endpoint for routines is /fire. Cloud sessions also get Anthropic's Claude Code Remote MCP server, which can schedule routines and start or steer other cloud sessions; it can be denied with permissions.deny entries such as mcp__Claude_Code_Remote.

findings.topic: Session-bound and local scheduling: /loop, CronCreate, Desktop tasks
findings.detail: /loop and CronCreate/CronList/CronDelete are session-scoped. Tasks fire only while Claude Code is running and idle. Recurring tasks expire after 7 days. A session holds at most 50 tasks. Recurring tasks can start up to 30 minutes late (jitter). On --resume, unexpired tasks are restored except self-paced loops. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 turns the scheduler off. Not suitable for 24/7 work. Desktop scheduled tasks run on the owner's machine only while the Desktop app is open and the computer is awake (the 'Keep computer awake' setting helps). Missed runs get one catch-up run within 7 days. In Manual permission mode a task stalls on permission prompts until approved. Neither option runs on a VPS.

findings.topic: Other subscription-side inbound routes for an always-on VPS
findings.detail: (1) claude -p 'message' --cloud <session-id> queues a message into an existing cloud session and exits. The docs list CI scripts as a use. It needs claude auth login on the sending machine and the org policy allow_remote_sessions. An idle VM restores on the next message, but an expired environment must be reopened by hand at claude.ai/code. (2) claude --cloud 'task' starts a new cloud session from the current repo (GitHub remote, or a bundle). (3) claude remote-control on the VPS runs a server that keeps local sessions alive for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise users. It needs a full claude.ai login (setup-token is not accepted), the machine must stay on, and sessions are driven from claude.ai or the app. No programmatic inbound API is documented. (4) Channels (research preview) push events into a running session. Included plugins are Telegram, Discord and iMessage, plus a fakechat demo. The session must stay open, --channels accepts only Anthropic-maintained or org-allowlisted plugins, and custom channels need --dangerously-load-development-channels, which is for testing. There is no WhatsApp channel, so this is not production-ready for WhatsApp.

findings.topic: Long-lived token: claude setup-token
findings.detail: claude setup-token creates a one-year OAuth token intended for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login is not possible. It requires a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests: it cannot run Remote Control or fetch claude.ai connectors (local MCP servers still work). It is ignored in --bare mode, which needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Precedence: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is 5th and subscription /login is 7th. The docs present this as a supported CI option, but the legal page's OAuth scope note still applies (see the legal findings).

findings.topic: Legal (a): explicitly supported on a subscription
findings.detail: Anthropic's product docs explicitly offer, on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise: scheduled cloud routines, /fire API-triggered routines, GitHub-triggered routines, RemoteTrigger for in-session management, and Desktop scheduled tasks (local only). Self-hosted routines are offered on Team and Enterprise (public beta). This product offering is the strongest evidence of permission I found. No document ties it to the Consumer Terms s.3 'explicitly permit' exception, and no document addresses business-scale always-on use specifically. Classification is my judgment.

findings.topic: Legal (b): gray area
findings.detail: (i) DIY scripts on the VPS using account login or setup-token: claude -p, --cloud and remote-control are documented, but the legal page says OAuth is 'intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code', and that Pro and Max advertised limits 'assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK'. (ii) Team and Enterprise fall under the Commercial Terms (effective date June 17, 2025 on the page I fetched). I found no automated-access bar there, and Section A.1 says Anthropic 'gives Customer permission to use the Services, including to power products and services'. The OAuth note still applies, so confirm with Anthropic. (iii) Agent SDK apps on subscription login: the SDK overview says 'Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK.' Internal use is gray; a product is not allowed.

findings.topic: Legal (c): not permitted
findings.detail: Consumer Terms s.3 (effective October 8, 2025): 'Except when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it,' you may not 'access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise.' The Consumer Terms introduction says the Commercial Terms govern API keys and Console but: 'For clarity, this does not include Claude.ai or Claude Pro use for individuals or entities.' My reading is that Pro use by a business is governed by the Consumer Terms, so unofficial automation on Pro or Max is barred unless Anthropic explicitly permits it. The legal page adds: developers building products or services should use API keys; Anthropic 'does not permit third-party developers to offer Claude.ai login into their own applications, or to route requests through Free, Pro, or Max plan credentials on behalf of their users'; developers 'may not collect, store, or intermediate Claude.ai credentials or session tokens'; and customers 'may not pay for, resell, or intermediate Claude usage on their end users' behalf'. Consumer Terms s.2 also bars sharing account login or API keys with anyone. If Ivinfotech sells this agent to clients, running it on subscription auth falls here.

findings.topic: Verified gaps in the docs
findings.detail: I did not find: a maximum run duration or concurrency cap for routines; a documented start-latency or SLA for /fire-created sessions; a routine-level notification setting; a documented way to create or delete routines from outside Claude (only /fire is external); SSH or raw TCP from cloud sessions; whether a routine can exist without a repository (the create steps say 'one or more repositories'; not tested); exact five-hour or weekly limits; Team and Enterprise pricing (not checked, not invented).

setup_steps: 1. Decide the plan first. Pro or Max gives cloud routines only. Team or Enterprise adds the self-hosted VPS option, but an Owner must turn on the Routines toggle (claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code) and, for the VPS, 'Allow self-hosted environments' (claude.ai/admin-settings/cloud-environments). Get Anthropic's written position (see open questions) before building anything that runs in production.

2. Prerequisites: sign in with claude.ai, not an API key (unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Connect GitHub (Claude GitHub App at github.com/apps/claude, or /web-setup), because each routine run clones a repo. Confirm claude.ai/code/routines opens.

3. Expose the CRM as HTTPS on a real domain with valid TLS (for example crm.example.com). Create a CRM API key that can only create or update proposal records with status pending_approval. Sending WhatsApp messages stays in Flask behind a human Approve button. Do not give routines any SSH key or shell path into the VPS.

4. Create a private GitHub repo (for example sales-ops) containing CLAUDE.md (rules: write proposals only, never send, cite sources), prompts/daily.md, prompts/urgent.md, and .claude/settings.json with permissions.deny for tools you do not need. Keep no secrets in the repo. Repo settings only take effect in single-repo sessions.

5. Create an environment named sales-ops at claude.ai/code. Set Network access to Custom with allowed domains crm.example.com and api.apify.com only, and do not choose Full. On Pro or Max, add the CRM key as a network secret for crm.example.com. On Team or Enterprise, use an env var in a shared environment visible only to you.

6. At claude.ai/customize/connectors keep only the connectors you need (Apify, if it is added there as a connector). Locally added 'claude mcp add' servers are not included in routines. In the routine form, remove every connector you do not need, because all connectors are included by default.

7. Daily routine: claude.ai/code/routines > New routine > name sales-daily. Write a self-contained prompt covering discovery, enrichment, grading, writing proposals via the CRM API, a one-line summary, and an explicit 'do not send anything' rule. Select the repo, the sales-ops environment and the connectors. Trigger: Schedule > Daily at 06:07. Confirm the timezone shows Asia/Kolkata (06:00 IST = 00:30 UTC; 06:07 IST = 00:37 UTC). Create it, then test with Run now first (Run now counts toward the 30-per-hour cap).

8. Urgent routine: New routine named sales-urgent. Its prompt says to act only on items inside the routine-fire-payload block. Each item has a WhatsApp message id, phone and text. The routine pulls lead history from the CRM, drafts a reply and proposal, writes them as pending_approval, and never sends. Use the same repo and environment with minimal connectors. Save it with no schedule. Then Edit > Add another trigger > API > copy the URL > Generate token. The token is shown once, so store it in a Flask environment variable.

9. Flask caller (keep URL and token in environment variables, not code): POST to the URL with Authorization: Bearer <token>, anthropic-version: 2023-06-01, anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 (send both until the docs agree), Content-Type: application/json, and body {"text": "<plain text, max 65536 characters>"}. Dedupe by WhatsApp message id before firing, because the endpoint has no idempotency. Batch messages that arrive within about 1-2 minutes into one fire (a design suggestion) to stay under 30 per hour. On 429, read Retry-After and requeue. On 5xx, back off and retry. Store the returned claude_code_session_url in the CRM for audit.

10. Owner alerts: end the daily prompt with a summary sent through a connector you trust (Slack or email, if connected), or have Flask message you after proposals appear in the CRM. Add a Flask watchdog that alerts if no daily run appears on claude.ai/code/routines by about 06:30 IST.

11. Keep usage predictable: check /usage in the CLI and claude.ai/settings/usage regularly. Keep usage credits off if you do not want metered overage. Keep the GitHub connection alive, because a 72-hour lapse turns the routine off.
12. Rollback: switch the routine off with its on/off toggle, or click Delete token to cut API access. Generating a new token revokes the old one.

13. Optional VPS-resident path (Team or Enterprise only): an Owner enables self-hosted environments. On a Linux VPS, create a dedicated non-root user and install Claude Code v2.1.224 or later. Create the environment in admin settings and copy the environment key. Save it with (umask 077 && cat > /etc/claude/environment-secret). Run claude self-hosted-runner --environment-secret-file /etc/claude/environment-secret --base-dir <dir> under systemd with Restart=always. Keep VPS secrets out of that user's environment, enforce default-deny egress, and route the routine to the environment from the routine's environment picker. The environment key expires after 365 days.
limits_and_risks: Schedule minimum is 1 hour. You cannot poll faster than hourly from a schedule. Sub-hour polling needs Flask-driven /fire calls, which are capped.
Caps: 30 fires per hour per routine (shared with Run now and API fires); 100 API fires per hour per account; 100 scheduled runs per hour per account. Over the API cap you get 429 with no queue.
No documented start-latency or SLA for /fire-created sessions. Scheduled runs can start several minutes late. Measure before promising WhatsApp reply times.
No idempotency on /fire. Webhook retries create duplicate sessions and duplicate proposals unless Flask dedupes by message id.
Each fire is a new session with no conversational memory. All state must live in the CRM.
Inbound WhatsApp text is untrusted. The routine wraps it as data, but included connectors with write access run without approval. Keep any send-capable connector out of the routine.

Subscription usage pool: routines share the same five-hour and weekly limits as interactive use. Exact caps were not published in the help article I read. The third-party 5/15/25-per-day figure is not in the official docs.
If usage credits are on, runs past the limit become metered overage. If off, runs are rejected until the window resets. A paused subscription holds routines.
Routines belong to one person's claude.ai account, not the team. If that person leaves or the GitHub connection lapses for 72 hours, routines stop or turn off.
Research preview: API shape, header requirements and limits may change. The docs disagree on whether the beta header is required.
Network: the Trusted default excludes your CRM, so you must add it. Full network access widens exfiltration risk if the agent is prompt-injected. Raw SSH to a VPS is not documented as possible.

Pro and Max have no documented shell or SSH access to your VPS. Only Team or Enterprise self-hosted runners execute on your host, and that is public beta, Linux or macOS only, and sessions can read any credential on the runner host.

Self-hosted limits: an org IP allowlist breaks Anthropic-hosted sessions (self-hosted sessions call the API from your network); orgs with Zero Data Retention or HIPAA cannot self-host; the environment key expires after 365 days.
Desktop scheduled tasks and /loop are local or session-bound and are not 24/7. Channels have no WhatsApp plugin and need an open session.

Legal: Consumer Terms s.3 bars automated access on Pro or Max except via API key or where Anthropic explicitly permits it. The Claude Code legal page says OAuth is for ordinary use. Serving clients on subscription auth is prohibited. Internal use is gray. Not legal advice; get Anthropic's written position.
result.verdict: Partly. Routines are viable for two things: a daily 06:07 IST batch routine that writes proposals to the CRM, and low-volume urgent API fires where a few minutes of latency is acceptable and the CRM holds all state. They are not viable as the always-on operator on their own: there is no sub-hour polling, no documented latency SLA, no documented SSH or shell access to your VPS on Pro or Max, no WhatsApp channel, and no conversational memory across messages. The only documented VPS-resident option is a self-hosted environment, which needs a Team or Enterprise plan (pricing not checked) and is public beta. On legal grounds, the subscription routes are product-supported, but nothing I found confirms that business-scale always-on use is covered by Consumer Terms s.3, and DIY VPS scripts are gray. Get Anthropic's written position before production, and do not use subscription auth to serve other companies.
open_questions: Anthropic's written position (contact-sales link on the legal page) on whether always-on internal business automation via routines /fire, and via claude -p or setup-token on a VPS, falls within Consumer Terms s.3 'explicitly permit' and the OAuth 'ordinary use' note. Does Team or Enterprise change this?
Measured start latency from a /fire call to a running session. Is it seconds or minutes?
Can a routine exist with no GitHub repository? The docs say 'one or more repositories', but I did not test it.
Can a cloud session reach a VPS over SSH, or only HTTPS? Test only against a non-production host with Custom network access.
Does claude -p --cloud <session-id> reliably wake an idle session, and when does environment expiry block that?
Team and Enterprise pricing, and whether self-hosted environments are included in the plan (not checked; not invented here).
Is there any documented way for an external system, not a Claude session, to create or update routines? Only /fire is documented externally.
Current exact five-hour and weekly subscription limits for routine load, which the official help article does not publish.

result.summary: Anthropic documents several subscription-backed features that run without someone at the keyboard. Routines (Anthropic-hosted, schedule or HTTP-triggered) are the closest fit to a WhatsApp-webhook-driven agent. Desktop scheduled tasks need an awake computer with the app open. Remote Control and official Channels need a live local claude process. CI and script use is covered by a one-year setup-token that the docs describe for “CI pipelines, scripts”. None of these is an explicit permission for an always-on company sales agent that messages prospects on a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise seat. The terms allow subscription OAuth only for “ordinary use”, say agents built for others must use API keys, and bar automated access unless Anthropic “explicitly permit[s] it”. Capacity is not published: Pro and Max share 5-hour and weekly windows with chat, and routine runs are rejected once those are used up unless usage credits are on. Verdict: partly viable as a gray-area pilot; get Anthropic's answer in writing before production.

findings.topic: Consumer Terms: automated-access clause (Free, Pro, Max)
findings.detail: Section 3, item 7 says: “Except when you are accessing our Services via an Anthropic API Key or where we otherwise explicitly permit it, to access the Services through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise.” The preamble says the terms govern “Claude.ai, Claude Pro, and other products and services that we may offer for individuals.” Section 2: “You may not share your Account login information, Anthropic API key, or Account credentials with anyone else” and “You also may not make your Account available to anyone else.” Section 12 lets Anthropic “increase or decrease capacity limits”; no numeric usage limit is stated. Unattended subscription use therefore depends on an explicit permission from Anthropic, which is the decisive question.

findings.topic: Claude Code legal page: what subscription OAuth is for (applies to Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise)
findings.detail: “OAuth authentication is intended exclusively for purchasers of Claude Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscription plans and is designed to support ordinary use of Claude Code and other native Anthropic applications.” “Advertised usage limits for Pro and Max plans assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK.” “Developers building products or services that interact with Claude's capabilities, including those using the Agent SDK, should use API key authentication.” It also says “Anthropic reserves the right to take measures to enforce these restrictions and may do so without prior notice,” and for questions about permitted auth methods to “contact sales.” Moving from Pro to Team does not remove the ‘ordinary use’ language.

findings.topic: Which contract governs which plan
findings.detail: The Claude Code legal page says Free, Pro and Max users are under the Consumer Terms, and Team, Enterprise and API users are under the Commercial Terms. The Commercial Terms page covers “Anthropic API keys and any other Anthropic offerings that references these Terms”, says “Services under these Terms are not for consumer use”, and does not mention Claude Code, Team or subscriptions. The Consumer Terms include the notice “For clarity, this does not include Claude.ai or Claude Pro use for individuals or entities.” A company running on a Pro seat therefore sits in a gap the terms do not resolve. Team or Enterprise has the clearer contract basis, but the OAuth ‘ordinary use’ language still applies.

findings.topic: Agents for your own company vs agents for customers
findings.detail: (a) Internal use via API key: the legal page says configuring an API key “for use by the customer's own authorized users” is not restricted, as long as usage is billed to the key owner. (b) Products for customers via API: Commercial Terms A.1 covers “products and services Customer makes available to its own customers and end users.” (c) Products for customers on subscriptions: each end user must sign in with their own API key or subscription, and the company may not pay for, resell or intermediate Claude usage for end users. (d) Agent SDK: “Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods...” No Anthropic page addresses a company's own internal, always-on agent running on a subscription login. That gap is where this use case sits.

findings.topic: Routines (cloud): explicitly supported unattended path
findings.detail: Routines “execute on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure... so they keep working when your laptop is closed.” Available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise; research preview. Triggers: schedule (hourly minimum), API (HTTP POST to a per-routine /fire endpoint with a bearer token and optional text), and GitHub events. Each fire starts a new session; sessions are not reused. Runs draw down subscription usage. There is no permission-mode picker: the run executes shell and connectors “without stopping for approval”. All connected claude.ai connectors are included by default, and “Claude can use every tool from an included connector, including writes, without asking.” A fired prompt is “not live user input and can't act as approval or consent for actions during the run.” Cloud sessions use subscription credentials, and an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set in the cloud environment does not override them. The /fire endpoint is documented as a way to wire Claude into “alerting systems, deploy pipelines, internal tools”, which matches a Flask server calling it.

findings.topic: Routines: caps, timing and network
findings.detail: Hourly caps: scheduled runs 100 per hour per account (they wait when over the limit); Run now, API fires and one-off reruns 30 per hour per routine, one shared count (they fail when over); API fires 100 per hour per account. None of these has overage. Schedules set on the exact hour can start several minutes late, so the docs suggest an off-hour minute such as 9:07. Default environment uses Trusted network access, which allows only a default package allowlist; other hosts return 403 host_not_allowed until you switch the environment to Custom and add domains. Connectors are routed through Anthropic and need no allowlist entry. Routine start latency after a fire is not documented.

findings.topic: Desktop scheduled tasks and Cowork (local, on your computer)
findings.detail: Desktop scheduled tasks run on your machine with access to local files: “A local task ... only fires while the app is open and your computer is awake.” If the computer sleeps through a scheduled time the run is skipped. Missed runs within 7 days produce one catch-up run on wake. Keep computer awake is a setting. A run that needs a permission it does not have “stalls until you approve it.” Dispatch (Cowork) takes tasks from the phone, requires Pro or Max, needs Desktop open and the computer awake, and auto-denies unanswered approvals after ten minutes. The Desktop docs say Dispatch and computer use are not available on Team or Enterprise. The Cowork changelog (v2.37337.1, 2026-10-13, and earlier entries) refers to scheduled tasks that can be moved to the cloud, and to automatic re-runs after 5, 15 and 30 minutes when the model cannot be reached. Windows Server is not listed as a supported Desktop platform.

findings.topic: Remote Control (steering a live local session, not event-driven)
findings.detail: Requires a claude.ai login; “API keys are not supported”, and a setup-token “can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions”. The local claude process must keep running (“start it inside tmux or screen” on a remote Linux machine). Server mode (claude remote-control) asks a one-time “Enable Remote Control? (y/n)” and a workspace-trust question, so a headless box needs one interactive first run. The connection is outbound HTTPS only. After an extended network outage server mode exits after about 10 minutes; a stopped server's sessions can be brought back for about four hours. Team and Enterprise Owners must turn it on, and it is off by default there. It is unavailable on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, behind a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, and under ZDR or HIPAA. Permission prompts can be answered from the phone. It gives no way to inject an external event such as a webhook.

findings.topic: CI, scripts and claude setup-token (one-year subscription token)
findings.detail: Docs: “For CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available, generate a one-year OAuth token with claude setup-token.” Set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. The token “authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan. It can only make model requests, so it can't establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors. MCP servers you configure locally still work.” Bare mode (--bare) does not read it and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set and approved, it takes precedence over the subscription, so an accidental key bills the API. The authentication page also warns that unattended sessions that outlive the login stop making progress until you sign in again, and that the login warning appears three days before expiry (the total duration is not stated in the pages read).

findings.topic: GitHub Actions: Anthropic's documented scheduled subscription-token example
findings.detail: The GitHub Actions page says: “If you authenticate with an OAuth token, runs use your Claude subscription instead of API billing.” It includes a cron example (“Run on a schedule”) and says the action runs “on any GitHub event”. It advises an API key instead of an OAuth token for secrets shared across repositories, “since an OAuth token is tied to the subscription of the person who ran claude setup-token.” Jobs run on GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runners and consume Actions minutes. Scheduled workflows in public repos are disabled after 60 days without activity. This is the most explicit Anthropic example of an unattended subscription job, but it is still a CI pattern.

findings.topic: Headless claude -p: unattended controls
findings.detail: claude -p runs non-interactively. --permission-mode dontAsk denies anything that would prompt; --permission-prompts none (v2.1.259+) tells a run not to wait for an answer; --allowedTools pre-approves specific tools. Background work is waited on for up to 10 minutes by default (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS changes this). Without --bare, a -p run loads project hooks and MCP servers without a trust dialog. The Fable model: “When a Fable request there would bill to usage credits, Claude Code bills it without asking” in -p mode.

findings.topic: Channels: official vs custom (WhatsApp)
findings.detail: A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into a running session. Channels need claude.ai or Console API-key auth. Official research-preview plugins are Telegram, Discord, iMessage and fakechat; there is no WhatsApp plugin. The session must stay open. Pro and Max users opt in per session with --channels; Team and Enterprise Owners must enable channels first. Custom channels are not on the allowlist and run only with --dangerously-load-development-channels, which the docs describe as “to test locally”. It shows a full-screen confirmation, is ignored under -p and the Agent SDK, and the docs say “Don't use it to run channels from untrusted sources.” Production listing needs an Anthropic partner contact, or an org allowlist on Team/Enterprise. A WhatsApp webhook channel in production is therefore not a supported path today.

findings.topic: Self-hosted environments (Team/Enterprise public beta): the only documented way for a routine to reach your network
findings.detail: An Owner turns on “Allow self-hosted environments” (off by default). A runner on your infrastructure polls api.anthropic.com over outbound HTTPS, clones the repo, and starts a Claude Code child process. Routines can be routed to these environments. The control plane stays on Anthropic. Sessions authenticate with an Anthropic-issued, session-scoped OAuth token and consume your organization's Claude Code usage. ZDR and HIPAA organizations are excluded. The docs cover Kubernetes and Compose deployments; Windows runner support is not confirmed in the pages read. This would give a routine access to the VPS without a public endpoint.

findings.topic: Subscription usage limits and what happens at the limit
findings.detail: Pro and Max have a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit, shared across Claude and Claude Code. Max has a separate weekly Fable limit. Pricing-page wording: Pro gets at least 5x Free's usage per 5-hour session; Max 5x and 20x give 5x or 20x Pro's usage per 5-hour session. No prompt counts or hours per window are published. At the limit, “Claude Code blocks further requests until the reset time shown in the message.” The wait-and-continue behavior is described for interactive sessions only; the docs do not say how -p or routines behave at the limit beyond rejecting runs. Usage credits are metered overage on the same account. On Pro and Max, the usage-credits row shows “Unlimited” with no spend figure when no monthly limit is set. Max's monthly API credits “can't be used in Claude Code or the Claude apps.” Fable can “bill to usage credits instead of drawing on your plan's included limits.”

findings.topic: Team and Enterprise usage model
findings.detail: Each member has a per-seat allowance on rolling five-hour and weekly windows, shared with Claude chat and Cowork. Size depends on Standard or Premium seat (Premium is described as 5x Standard). Usage credits and spend limits can be set at organization, group or member level. Enterprise usage “scales with model and task.” Routines belong to an individual claude.ai account and their runs count against that account, so the docs do not describe a service or automation seat.

findings.topic: Plan prices (as displayed on the pricing page, undated)
findings.detail: Pro: $17 per month on annual billing ($200 billed up front), $20 billed monthly. Max 5x and Max 20x: “From $100” per month. Team Standard seat: $20 per seat per month annual, $25 monthly. Team Premium seat: $100 annual, $125 monthly. Enterprise: “US$20/seat/month, billed annually” plus usage. Check the live page at checkout, since the page shows no date.

findings.topic: Claude Tag (Slack): not subscription-included for channel work
findings.detail: Claude Tag channel work bills to the organization's usage balance, capped by a spend limit that is set in advance. Team plans must fund the balance before Claude responds in channels. One-to-one DMs from members with a Claude account bill to that member's seat. Warnings post at 75% and 90% of the limit. When the limit is hit, Claude stops and tells the requester. This is a pay-as-you-go path, not seat allowance, and it is in public beta.

findings.topic: Capacity: what can and cannot be measured
findings.detail: No published token or prompt counts per window exist in the docs read. The measurable tools are the /usage screen (plan usage bars, and a Loops breakdown that shows how often each scheduled task ran and its tokens per run; press d or w to switch between 24 hours and 7 days) and claude.ai/settings/usage. The costs page notes that scheduled tasks fire on their interval even while idle and resend the full context each time, and that the subscription prompt-cache lifetime is one hour. Its only dollar figures are list-price averages for Claude Code developers (about $13 per active day; $150–250 per developer per month), which are a rough proxy, not subscription capacity. Inference: a few hours of tool-heavy work per day will likely span several 5-hour windows and press on the weekly cap on Pro; measure before committing.

findings.topic: Windows Server 2022 host
findings.detail: The setup page lists “Windows 10 1809+ or Windows Server 2019+” for Claude Code, so the CLI installs on this host. Git for Windows is recommended for the Bash tool; without it, the PowerShell tool is used. The Desktop docs read do not list Windows Server, and do not say whether the Desktop app needs an interactive logged-in session. Keeping a claude process alive on Windows is not documented (tmux and screen are Linux tools), so a Windows service or Task Scheduler setup would be a custom design, not an Anthropic-documented one.

setup_steps: Check the plan and login. Run /status in Claude Code and confirm a claude.ai subscription login. Remove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN from the shell and from any settings.json env block, so nothing bills to the API by accident. The docs say an approved API key takes precedence over the subscription.

Get a written answer from Anthropic before building production. The legal page says to contact sales about permitted authentication methods (https://www.anthropic.com/contact-sales). Ask: may an unattended internal agent on a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise subscription send messages to third parties (prospects) on the company's behalf, and may one account serve several staff? If the answer is no, the API-key route is the only documented one.

If on Team or Enterprise, ask the Owner to confirm the Routines toggle at https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code. Remote Control and channels also need Owner enablement there if used. Routines can be turned off for the whole organization.

Connect only the services the routine needs at https://claude.ai/customize/connectors. Routines include every connector by default and can write without asking, so remove the rest. Local MCP servers added with claude mcp add are not connectors and will not appear in routines: re-add them as claude.ai connectors, or commit a .mcp.json in the repo the routine clones.

Create a private repository that holds the playbook (CLAUDE.md with sales rules, approval rules and forbidden actions). Routines are built around one or more repositories, each cloned at the start of every run. Confirm in the form whether a routine can be saved with no repository.
