Create a cloud environment with Custom network access that allows only your CRM's HTTPS domain, keeping the default package list. Put secrets in network secrets (Pro and Max), not plain environment variables, since environment variables are visible to everyone who uses the environment.

Create the routine at https://claude.ai/code/routines (or run /schedule in the CLI). Write a self-contained prompt: the goal, the data sources (the CRM API), the output format, what to write back to the CRM, and what never to do. If the fire text is used, say so explicitly in the prompt, because the docs wrap it as untrusted data. Select a specific model. Do not select Fable unless you accept usage-credit billing.

Add a schedule trigger for daily discovery or enrichment (hourly minimum, use an off-hour minute such as 9:07). Then add an API trigger: Edit the routine, Select a trigger, Add another trigger, API, Generate token. The token is shown once, so store it in the CRM's secret store.

In the Flask CRM, add one function that sends an HTTPS POST to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/claude_code/routines/<routine-id>/fire with headers Authorization: Bearer <token>, anthropic-beta: experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 and anthropic-version: 2023-06-01. The body is a small JSON object whose text field holds only a lead or event ID. The routine reads the details from the CRM API. The response includes claude_code_session_url for monitoring. Note that the docs say this endpoint is for claude.ai users, is not part of the Platform API, and its beta header may change.

Enforce approvals in the CRM, not in the prompt. The send endpoint should refuse any outbound message that lacks an approved draft record and an owner approval flag, and should log who approved and when. The docs say a fired prompt cannot act as approval, so the gate must live in your backend.

Measure before relying on it. Fire a test and time fire-to-session-start (not documented, so measure it). For a week, check the /usage Loops rows and https://claude.ai/settings/usage daily to see per-run token cost and window consumption. Compare the numbers against the hourly caps and the 5-hour and weekly windows.
Keep usage credits off. If you turn them on, first set a monthly spend limit at https://claude.ai/settings/usage, because the docs show ‘Unlimited’ when no limit is set.

Only if Anthropic confirms subscription-based unattended use in writing: on a PC with a browser run claude setup-token, put the result into CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on the VPS, make sure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset, run claude -p without --bare, pre-approve tools with --allowedTools or --permission-mode dontAsk, and expect no Remote Control and no claude.ai connectors with that token.

Do not build the production path on: a custom WhatsApp channel run with --dangerously-load-development-channels, Agent SDK services using subscription login (the docs say to use API keys), or Remote Control or Desktop scheduled tasks as the event trigger. Each is either documented as test-only or not designed for unattended operation.
limits_and_risks: Research preview: Routines and Channels are research previews and their behavior, limits and API surface may change. The /fire endpoint sits behind an experimental beta header that the docs say may change.

Hourly caps (Routines): 100 scheduled runs per account per hour; 30 per routine per hour shared across Run now, API fires and one-off reruns; 100 API fires per account per hour. There is no overage on these caps. The schedule minimum is one hour.

Subscription windows: Pro and Max share five-hour and weekly windows with chat, Cowork and Claude Code. When they run out, routine runs are rejected until the window resets, unless usage credits are on. Team and Enterprise seat allowances are also shared with chat and Cowork.
Usage credits are metered overage on the same account. With no monthly spend limit, the docs show ‘Unlimited’. An always-on agent with credits on and no cap is an open-ended spend risk.
Fable: outside interactive sessions the docs describe Fable requests billing usage credits, and in -p mode they bill without asking. Pin an explicit non-Fable model for unattended jobs.

No approval step inside a routine: connector writes happen without asking, and actions appear under the owner's identity (commits and connector actions use the owner's linked accounts). The approval gate must be enforced by the CRM backend.
Routines start a new session per trigger and do not reuse conversation state, so context must come from the CRM or the repo on every run.

Network: the default Trusted allowlist blocks other hosts (403 host_not_allowed). A private VPS is reachable from a cloud routine only if it exposes an HTTPS endpoint you allow, or if you use a self-hosted environment (Team/Enterprise). SSH from a cloud routine is not documented.

Desktop scheduled tasks skip runs when the machine sleeps, stall on unapproved permissions until someone answers, and run a single catch-up for missed slots. Dispatch auto-denies unanswered approvals after ten minutes.

Remote Control and any process-based setup: a machine must stay on and the claude process must keep running. Server mode exits after about ten minutes of network outage. An unattended session that outlives its login stops making progress until you sign in again. The docs warn three days before expiry, but the total login duration is not stated in the pages read.
setup-token: one-year token, model requests only (no Remote Control, no claude.ai connectors). Bare mode ignores it. An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, if present and approved, takes precedence and bills the API.

Channels: there is no official WhatsApp plugin. A custom channel needs the development flag, which the docs describe as for testing, shows a confirmation dialog at launch, and is ignored under -p and the SDK. The docs do not say whether the confirmation is remembered between launches.
Enforcement: the legal page says Anthropic may enforce its auth restrictions “without prior notice”. Consumer Terms section 12 lets Anthropic change capacity limits.
Account sharing: one subscription login used by several staff or by a shared automation may fall under the account-sharing clause (Consumer Terms section 2).
Product naming and availability are in flux: the pricing page says “Claude Cowork is now just Claude”, rolling out to Pro and Max; Dispatch and computer use are not available on Team or Enterprise.
Claude Tag channel work is metered to a funded usage balance, not seat allowance. Team plans must fund it before anything runs. It is not a subscription-included path for channel work.
Capacity is unpublished for the owner's workload. Any capacity estimate must come from measurement (the /usage Loops breakdown and claude.ai usage page) rather than from the docs.
result.verdict: Partly. The features exist and are documented. Routines are an Anthropic-hosted, subscription-billed agent that can run on a schedule or be fired by an authenticated HTTP call from a Flask server, which is close to the event-driven pattern described. But the terms do not explicitly permit a subscription to power an always-on company sales agent that messages prospects. Subscription OAuth is documented for “ordinary use”. Agents built for others must use API keys. The automated-access clause allows unattended access only where Anthropic explicitly permits it. The CI and script setup-token wording is the nearest explicit permission, and it is not a 24/7 business-operations permission. Capacity is not published, and routine runs are rejected once the windows are exhausted unless usage credits are on. Treat the subscription path as a gray-area pilot: get written confirmation from Anthropic first, use Routines as the only unattended entry point (ideally on a Team or Enterprise account), keep the CRM as the approval gate, and measure real usage before committing. If Anthropic says no, the only path the terms explicitly bless for this use is an API key, which the owner has ruled out. Remote Control, official Channels and Desktop scheduled tasks are real features, but they are built for steering or for a machine kept awake, not for event-driven 24/7 operation, and a custom WhatsApp channel is not a supported production path.
open_questions: Does Anthropic explicitly permit an unattended internal sales agent that messages third parties on a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise subscription? No page answers this, and the legal page directs such questions to sales (https://www.anthropic.com/contact-sales).
How long does a routine take from a /fire call to a running session? Latency is not documented and decides whether the ‘within minutes’ requirement is met.
Can a routine be saved with zero repositories? The docs describe a routine as a prompt plus one or more repositories, but do not say whether zero is allowed.
Can a cloud routine reach a VPS over SSH, or only over HTTPS? Only HTTPS fire and HTTPS egress are documented.
Can a Team or Enterprise seat serve as an automation identity for routines, or must it be a person's account? Routines belong to an individual claude.ai account and no page covers service seats.
Does the Desktop app or Cowork run scheduled tasks on Windows Server 2022, and does it need an interactive logged-in session? The Desktop docs list no server SKU.
How long does a claude.ai login last before it must be renewed with /login? The docs warn three days before expiry but do not state the total duration in the pages read.
What is the actual per-window capacity for the owner's workload? No published figures exist; measure with /usage and claude.ai/settings/usage over at least a week.
What runtime and limits apply to Cowork scheduled tasks that have been moved to the cloud? Only changelog entries mention this feature (v2.26454.0 and v2.37337.1).
Do fire requests to /fire have an IP allowlist or other source restrictions? Not documented in the pages read.

result.summary: Research date 2026-10-14. Running the official Claude Code binary 24/7 on a Linux VPS under a subscription login is technically doable and is what most practitioners do (tmux, or systemd supervising tmux, running claude interactively with a Telegram/Discord channel or Remote Control). It is not a documented, supported always-on product. Anthropic documents building blocks for this (Channels, Remote Control, background sessions, Routines, /loop, setup-token) but labels several as research preview. In practice the weak points are channel/session lifecycle bugs (many closed as not planned by a stale-bot, with no maintainer reply), headless OAuth refresh failures, permission prompts that stall a session, usage caps, and memory growth in long sessions. On terms: the line Anthropic has actually drawn is against using subscription credentials inside third-party products and harnesses (enforced from January 2026, and by billing since 2026-04-04). Running the unmodified official binary is allowed, but Anthropic says plan limits assume ordinary individual use. It also says developers building products or services, including on the Agent SDK, should use API keys. Whether an unattended business sales operator on Pro/Max is ordinary use is unresolved. No source explicitly permits it and no credible source shows it was punished. I found no independent multi-month production case study (Reddit could not be searched). A subscription-powered operator is realistic for a small business only as a best-effort component: the CRM database must be the source of truth with a durable inbound queue, the agent needs a layered watchdog, risky actions must be gated outside the model, and the owner must accept account-level risk that Anthropic can suspend without notice. Obtaining written confirmation from Anthropic for this use is the one step that would remove the largest uncertainty.

findings.topic: Terms (a) EXPLICITLY SUPPORTED on a subscription
findings.detail: Documented by Anthropic and tied to a claude.ai subscription login: (1) interactive Claude Code, signed in via OAuth; the legal page says OAuth is intended for ordinary use of Claude Code and native Anthropic apps, and that an end user may sign in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription, including where a platform hosts it. (2) Remote Control (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise; API keys unsupported; claude remote-control server mode exists). (3) Background sessions via claude --bg / claude agents (research preview; sessions keep running without a terminal; do not survive reboot). (4) Channels (research preview): Pro/Max individuals can use them with the --channels flag; Team/Enterprise need an Owner to enable channelsEnabled. (5) Routines (research preview; cloud; schedule min 1h; API /fire trigger; draws subscription usage). (6) /loop and desktop scheduled tasks. (7) claude setup-token, described as a one-year token for CI/scripts that authenticates against the subscription (model requests only). (8) Help Center, still current after the 2026-06-15 pause and an Oct 7 2026 update: Agent SDK, claude -p and third-party app usage draw from subscription limits. Note: that last point is a billing statement; it is not an explicit grant of permission under the Consumer Terms automation clause.

findings.topic: Terms (b) GRAY AREA
findings.detail: Consumer Terms Section 3 item 7 bars accessing the Services by automated or non-human means (bot, script, or otherwise) unless via an Anthropic API key or where Anthropic otherwise explicitly permits it. Nothing I found names cron, claude -p, tmux, VPS or channel bridges as permitted or forbidden. Claude Code docs themselves document claude -p in scripts/CI and /loop, and a staff member said in Feb 2026 (via X, reported by secondary press) that nothing changed for Agent SDK and Max and that Anthropic wants to encourage local development and experimentation with the Agent SDK and claude -p. Unresolved cases: (i) cron or webhook triggering claude -p on a VPS; (ii) a chat-bridge that pipes inbound third-party messages into claude -p or a channel; (iii) 24/7 unattended interactive sessions; (iv) business use on a consumer (Pro/Max) plan: the legal page says advertised Pro/Max limits assume ordinary, individual usage of Claude Code and the Agent SDK, and that developers building products or services, including via the Agent SDK, should use API keys; (v) an agent that autonomously messages your customers or prospects may be read as running a service. HN commenters list exactly these cases as the unresolved ambiguity. The legal page invites contacting sales about permitted authentication methods for a specific use case.

findings.topic: Terms (c) PROHIBITED (clearly stated)
findings.detail: Per the Claude Code legal page: third-party developers may not offer claude.ai login in their apps or route requests through Free/Pro/Max credentials on behalf of users; developers may not collect, store or intermediate claude.ai credentials or session tokens; hosts must run the unmodified binary and may not pay for, resell or intermediate Claude usage on end users' behalf; Anthropic may enforce without prior notice. Per The Register (Feb 20 2026), using OAuth tokens obtained from Free/Pro/Max in any other product, tool or service is not permitted. Consumer Terms: no sharing account login or credentials, and Anthropic may suspend or terminate access at any time without notice. Automated access is barred except via API key or where Anthropic otherwise explicitly permit it (Consumer Terms s.3 item 7, quoted: where we otherwise explicitly permit it). Practical reading: extracting the OAuth token and using it from your own code/HTTP client or from a third-party agent framework is the clearly banned pattern; running Anthropic's own binary is not.

findings.topic: Billing and limit status timeline (verify before committing)
findings.detail: 2026-01-09: Anthropic tightened server-side safeguards against third-party harnesses spoofing Claude Code (reported via a staff post on X); some accounts were auto-banned by abuse filters and Anthropic said the known erroneous bans were lifted. 2026-02-19/20: legal page reworded; staff called it a docs cleanup. 2026-04-04: subscription limits stopped covering third-party harnesses (OpenClaw first); they must use extra usage or an API key; Anthropic spokesperson said such use is not permitted under the Terms; Claude.ai, Claude Code and Cowork remain covered. 2026-05-13/14: Anthropic announced that Agent SDK, claude -p, GitHub Actions and SDK-based apps would move to a separate monthly credit from 2026-06-15 (Pro $20, Max 5x $100, Max 20x $200). 2026-06-15/16: that change was paused; Help Center says nothing has changed and no separate credit exists. 2026-10-07 (Help Center update): Max and Team plans now include monthly API credits ($100 Max 5x, $200 Max 20x, Team pooled up to $500) usable for the Claude API, Managed Agents and Agent SDK, but explicitly NOT for Claude Code; when exhausted, requests stop (no charge to the plan). Anthropic said it is reworking the plan and will give advance notice of future change. Risk: the rules have changed four times in nine months.

findings.topic: OpenClaw: what it is and Anthropic's stance
findings.detail: OpenClaw is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed autonomous agent run on your own machine and driven through messaging apps (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.). Created by Peter Steinberger; first published Nov 24 2025 as Warelay, then Clawdbot, renamed Moltbot on Jan 27 2026 after Anthropic trademark complaints, then OpenClaw on Jan 30 2026; Steinberger announced joining OpenAI on Feb 14 2026 with a non-profit foundation to steward the project. Anthropic stance: it is a third-party harness, so since 2026-04-04 subscription limits do not cover it. OpenClaw's own docs now say its Claude CLI backend (claude -p style reuse of the installed, logged-in official binary) is sanctioned for that integration and that an Anthropic API key is still the most predictable choice for an always-on gateway host; this is OpenClaw's statement, and I found no Anthropic page confirming it. Security record is poor (prompt-injection payload targeting OpenClaw agents found circulating in the wild, lab exfiltration demos, malicious skills). Hermes Agent (Nous Research) is a comparable assistant with an experimental plugin that shells out to the installed Claude Code CLI.

findings.topic: Enforcement evidence
findings.detail: Confirmed by Anthropic: Jan 2026 crackdown on subscription use in third-party harnesses (with some wrongful bans reversed) and the Apr 2026 billing cut-off. Docs also show an account-on-hold error with a restricted/appeal page, so account-level action is a real mechanism. Anecdotal and unverified: one HN user says a single claude -p in a custom harness got a Max account banned and the appeal was denied; Daimon Legal (an Australian law firm that used OpenClaw daily and was suspended; the author is the aggrieved party and sells a bridge tool) says no clause or conduct was identified and enforcement looks selective. GitHub issues (#91411 Max 20x suspended a day after payment, others citing VPN or renewal) show unexplained suspensions of ordinary users with no maintainer reply and a reportedly unreliable appeal path. I found NO credible report of a ban attributed solely to running the unmodified official claude binary via tmux or cron on a VPS, but absence of evidence is weak here: Reddit could not be searched and suspension reasons are never disclosed. Anthropic says enforcement may occur without notice.

findings.topic: (1) Patterns people actually run
findings.detail: A. tmux + interactive claude --channels plugin:discord (or telegram) on a small Hetzner VPS, Pro plan, headless login via a setup-token generated on a Mac, memory as markdown files committed to a private git repo, access only via Tailscale, broad auto-approve rules; author reports it rock solid but gives no uptime duration (about $26/month total). B. systemd user unit (with linger) -> watchdog loop every 30s -> tmux -> claude --remote-control, with spawn verification, health re-checks, 6h idle refresh, backoff and answers to first-run dialogs (claude-tmux-service); no stated production duration. C. systemd per-project claude units resumed with --continue, a systemd-timer watchdog, and a Telegram bridge that carries the /login flow (pocket-agents); very immature repo (0 stars, 20 commits). D. Webhook -> small bridge -> claude -p per inbound message, file-based per-customer state, systemd on a VPS (whatsapp-agent): closest to Ivinfotech's need; thin docs, no ToS or rate-limit notes, inconsistent cost claims. E. Cron-launched fresh claude sessions with on-disk state (BUILD_SPEC.md + PROGRESS.md + git), hourly overnight; works for coding builds, no rate-limit handling described. F. WhatsApp via unofficial Baileys channel plugins: carries WhatsApp-side ban risk, irrelevant if you use an official BSP. G. Anthropic's own built-ins: Routines, /loop, desktop scheduled tasks, agent view. No independent evidence of any of these running unattended for months; treat all uptime claims as unverified.

findings.topic: (2a) Pitfall: channel goes deaf, lifecycle bugs
findings.detail: Reports (mostly macOS, Claude Code 2.1.81-2.1.110): after finishing a turn the session sits at the prompt and later Telegram/Discord messages reach the MCP server but never start a turn (#38259, root-cause thread #36477); closed as not planned by a bot with no maintainer reply. Fixes users found: a watchdog that sends Escape+Enter to the tmux pane after N idle minutes (reported to fix about 80%), hard restart with --continue after more than 10 idle minutes, and bypassing the plugin by registering the server in .mcp.json and launching with the development-channels flag (needs an auto-Enter on every launch because of the confirmation dialog). Regression in 2.1.283: daemonised --channels churned sessions every ~2 minutes and killed the plugin's MCP child, while 2.1.177 had held one session for weeks (#97701, open); workaround is pinning or rolling back the version and an external supervisor. Telegram allows one poller per token and a second Claude session with the plugin enabled SIGTERMs the live poller, leaving the bot permanently silent; a maintainer reproduced it on 2026-08-24, still open (#81571); fix is enabling the plugin only in the bot's project and never starting another claude with it. Also leaked 100%-CPU bun server.ts processes ignore SIGTERM (#81107). Current changelog shows a permission-relay fix in 2.1.290 and latest version about 2.1.299.

findings.topic: (2b) Pitfall: no TTY, restarts and first-run dialogs
findings.detail: Running a channels session under systemd with no terminal crashed within about 15-20s with a stdin/--print error (#40726, closed as duplicate of a headless/raw-mode crash). Practitioners therefore run claude inside tmux (a pty) and supervise tmux. A blog systemd unit that launches tmux new-session -d returns immediately, so systemd may be watching the launcher rather than claude and never restart on a claude crash; use a supervisor script that stays in the foreground and checks the pane. First-run gates (theme, folder trust, bypass warning, resume-size chooser, development-channel confirmation) block a fresh process and must be pre-accepted once or answered by matching menu text; channel dev-flag confirmation appears on every launch and the flag is ignored in -p mode. Remote Control server mode exits after about 10 minutes offline and idle claude sessions can be stopped by the agent-view supervisor after about an hour unless pinned. Auto-updater banners can confuse pane scrapers (set DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1).

findings.topic: (2c) Pitfall: auth expiry and headless OAuth refresh
findings.detail: Official docs: for unattended background sessions and Remote Control sessions, an expired login stops all progress and cannot recover until someone signs in again; Claude Code warns 3 days before expiry and /status shows an expired-login row (v2.1.210+). setup-token tokens cannot establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors (locally configured MCP servers still work) and bare mode ignores them. Community bug reports: non-interactive -p does not refresh an expired access token (#28827, closed as duplicate Mar 2026); refresh requests from headless Linux servers blocked by Cloudflare WAF with 403/429 leading to lockout, never acknowledged, closed by a bot (#47754); one user says a one-year setup-token still needed /login about every 8 hours (#36911, single report, closed not planned); multiple scheduled claude --print jobs under one account invalidating each other or a desktop login (#98693, open, filed Oct 1 2026; v2.1.81 fixed one concurrent-session case). Fixes in the field: keep exactly one process per credential directory (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), do not fan out parallel -p jobs, monitor login status and alert early, keep a documented re-login runbook (SSH URL-and-code flow, or a Telegram login bridge like pocket-agents), and expect to re-login occasionally. Some guides recommend an API key for server workloads for this reason.

findings.topic: (2d) Pitfall: permission prompts block the session
findings.detail: Official: if Claude hits a permission prompt while you are away the session pauses; channels that declare permission relay (v2.1.81+, hardened in 2.1.234) can forward Bash/Write/Edit approvals as yes/no plus a 5-letter id to allowlisted senders, first answer (terminal or remote) wins, and anyone who can reply can approve, so allowlist only trusted people; project-trust and MCP-consent dialogs are not relayed. Background sessions show a needs-input state and replying does not answer a dialog. Options: auto mode (a classifier reviews actions and blocks ones that look driven by hostile content; falls back to manual if unavailable), dontAsk mode (anything that would prompt is denied, so with explicit allow rules the session never hangs), --permission-prompts none for -p runs (v2.1.259+), or dangerously-skip-permissions (docs require a container/VM and non-root user). A community monitoring tool had a permission dialog sit unanswered for about 1,516 seconds with no alert because its detector only knew option-select footers (dispatcher #435, fixed in that project), which shows why a liveness-only watchdog is not enough. Telegram-style bridges without relay simply hang on prompts.

findings.topic: (2e) Pitfall: usage caps mid-day
findings.detail: Session (5-hour) and weekly limits apply at once and are shared across models; blocked requests resume at the shown reset. Official auto-continue (v2.1.234+) waits and resumes only in interactive claude.ai-login sessions, only if the reset is within 24 hours, not in Remote Control, background sessions or -p, re-arms at most twice, and ends if the process exits; a weekly limit can be days away so nothing resumes automatically. A StopFailure hook fires on rate_limit and authentication_failed but output is ignored (alerting only). One practitioner built Stop/StopFailure hooks to resume after the reset, but tested only with fake data. Running N agents in parallel burns quota about N times faster (official); the prompt cache lasts 5 minutes, so loop cadence matters; scheduled/background work consumes the same subscription pool as interactive use. Routines also have hourly run caps (100 scheduled, 30 per routine for API fires, 100 per account) and wait or reject when the subscription limit is hit unless usage credits are enabled. Limits have changed several times; do not hard-code windows.

findings.topic: (2f) Pitfall: context bloat and long-session health
findings.detail: Official: context compacts automatically; instructions given early in a conversation can be lost, so persistent rules belong in CLAUDE.md (which is guidance, not enforcement; use hooks to enforce) and /context shows usage; auto-compaction stops with an error if a single huge output refills the window. Long-lived interactive sessions are also a stability risk: GitHub #96378 (open, macOS, v2.1.278-2.1.283) documents sessions that after roughly 3-17 hours entered GC thrash or a spin where the UI ignores keys and SIGTERM, only kill -9 works, with some cases leaking thousands of zombie children; the reporter's workaround is restarting every 2-3 hours with /exit then --resume. A Telegram plugin retry loop on a revoked token grew memory about 0.2 GB/hour per server (claude-plugins-official #6308). Mitigation pattern: keep each session short-lived and disposable (scheduled recycle when idle, resume from disk or, better, start fresh and rebuild context from the database), and watch RSS, CPU and zombie count. Idle sessions do not consume quota per one vendor blog, but every turn re-sends the whole conversation.

findings.topic: (2g) Pitfall: prompt injection in an always-on, tool-rich agent
findings.detail: Anthropic's own channels reference says an ungated channel is a prompt-injection vector and requires sender allowlisting (gate on sender id, not room). Routines wrap API fire text as untrusted data and only act on it if the saved prompt says so, and a fired prompt cannot serve as approval for actions. Real-world incidents are mostly OpenClaw-class agents: an injection payload impersonating a system audit message circulating on Reddit/Discord/web pages (Feb-Mar 2026), a Promptfoo lab where a malicious web page made a permissive assistant read local documents, write a secrets handoff file and send false broadcast messages (Mar 12 2026), and malicious skills. I did not find a documented incident of exfiltration through an unattended official Claude Code session reading email or chat, but Claude Code-adjacent flaws exist (claude-code-action issue-to-code-injection chain, config-injection CVEs) per secondary reporting. For Ivinfotech, every inbound WhatsApp reply is untrusted text from an unknown sender by definition, so the sender-allowlist defence does not apply; defence must be architectural (see recommendations).

findings.topic: (3) Recommended watchdog / health-check / restart design (synthesis of the above; the canary layer is my inference)
findings.detail: Layer 1 host: systemd service (user or system, lingering enabled, Restart=always) whose ExecStart is a foreground supervisor script, not tmux new-session -d. Layer 2 liveness every 30s: tmux session and claude process exist; recreate with backoff doubling to 5 min (claude-tmux-service default). Layer 3 readiness: after spawn, require the expected banner or channel-registered status within about 60s, else kill and retry; answer only known safe first-run dialogs by matching text, never by position. Layer 4 end-to-end canary (inference, motivated by channels that are alive but deaf): every 5-10 min Flask enqueues a synthetic ping event; the agent must call a heartbeat tool on the CRM MCP server; no ack within N minutes triggers Escape+Enter nudge, then restart with --continue (community used about 10 idle minutes), then human alert. Layer 5 blocked-state detection: capture-pane scan for permission/needs-input dialogs; alert after 2-3 minutes rather than auto-approving. Layer 6 auth: poll claude auth status (JSON) or /status; alert before expiry; runbook for re-login. Layer 7 usage: StopFailure hook (rate_limit, authentication_failed, billing_error) writes a flag to the CRM; pause non-urgent jobs and notify. Layer 8 hygiene: planned recycle when idle (claude-tmux-service uses sessions older than 6h and quiet 30 min; #96378 users use 2-3h), RSS/zombie/disk thresholds, kill -9 fallback because SIGTERM can be ignored, orphan bun cleanup. Layer 9 external dead-man switch: the VPS pings an outside monitor; silence pages the owner. Pin the Claude Code version and update deliberately (regressions like 2.1.283 happen).

findings.topic: (4) Memory and state strategy that works for long-lived agents
findings.detail: Consensus across Anthropic and practitioners: the live session is disposable; durable state lives outside it. For Ivinfotech that means the Flask CRM database is the source of truth (leads, conversations, task queue, approvals, decision log, idempotency keys), exposed to the agent through a small local MCP server with narrow tools (claim_next_task, get_conversation, draft_reply, request_approval, log_decision, heartbeat) that enforces rules server-side. Use CLAUDE.md for short stable operating rules (auto memory loads only its first 200 lines or 25KB), skills for playbooks (loaded on demand, so they do not bloat context), .claude/rules for scoped rules, and hooks (PreToolUse, PermissionRequest) for anything that must be enforced, since CLAUDE.md is advisory. A SessionStart hook (matchers include resume and compact) can inject a compact state brief after every restart or compaction. Anthropic's long-running-agent pattern: progress log, machine-readable feature/task list that the agent may only flip status on, frequent git commits, init script. Overnight-loop practitioners: immutable spec plus append-only progress file, log decisions not just actions, commit granularity equals checkpoint granularity, and fence irreversible actions as needs-human. Main hazard after restart is stale or confabulated beliefs and double execution of side effects; record send-intent in the database before calling the WhatsApp BSP and make sends idempotent. Persona/memory markdown files committed to a private git repo is a common lightweight variant.

findings.topic: (5) Keeping humans in control: approval relay, kill switch, digest
findings.detail: Approval relay: use the channel permission relay for tool-level prompts (allowlisted owner only) and CRM-level approval for business actions: the send_whatsapp tool should refuse unless the CRM holds an approved record, so approval does not depend on the model behaving. Official remote controls: Remote Control from the Claude mobile app or claude.ai/code, with optional push notifications when actions are required; Notification hook events for permission_prompt and idle_prompt; agent view shows needs-input and sends notifications. Kill switch (no dedicated open-source implementation found; compose these and test them): (1) CRM flag agent_enabled=false checked by every MCP tool, instant and independent of Claude Code; (2) systemctl stop plus tmux kill-session; (3) disable the webhook or revoke the bot token; (4) CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 to stop /loop and cron tools; (5) claude stop for background sessions; (6) on Team/Enterprise an Owner can turn channels, Remote Control or routines off in admin settings; (7) sign out or revoke the login. Daily digest: a scheduled job (VPS cron or a Routine) that summarises from the database: sends, replies, pending approvals, errors, usage and login health. Staged autonomy: run draft-only/shadow mode first, review early runs closely, cap sends per day and per lead, treat anything uncertain as needs-human.

findings.topic: Event-driven options compared (WhatsApp webhook to agent within minutes)
findings.detail: Option 1 custom channel (officially documented webhook-receiver pattern): a small MCP server in the running session receives POSTs on 127.0.0.1 and pushes them as channel events; events queue and are delivered together when Claude is busy; Claude Code does not acknowledge them and drops them silently if the session is not running or the channel is not loaded; custom channels are not on the research-preview allowlist so they need the development flag with an interactive confirmation on each launch; Team/Enterprise need channelsEnabled. Option 2 Routines API trigger: a Flask POST to the /fire endpoint (beta header, per-routine bearer token, text payload wrapped as untrusted) starts a fresh cloud session in minutes; no machine to babysit, but each fire is a new session, hourly caps apply, network access is limited by environment settings, and it cannot reach a private VPS unless network access allows. Option 3 per-message claude -p from a bridge: simple and stateless (state in files/DB) but this is the pattern the HN thread flags as unclear and the one the one Telegram-bot ban anecdote resembles; -p does not refresh OAuth reliably and bare mode ignores the subscription login. Option 4 poll: /loop or Claude polls the CRM every few minutes; works but 7-day expiry for recurring loop tasks, fires only when the session is idle, and no catch-up. Telegram-style plugins also lose messages when the session is down (one vendor blog claims Telegram retains for up to 24h; Discord and iMessage do not), so Flask must hold the durable queue and re-deliver.

findings.topic: Included API credits as a separate officially supported path
findings.detail: Since Oct 7 2026 Max 5x/20x and Team plans include monthly Console API credits ($100, $200, Team up to $500 pooled) that can run the Claude API, Managed Agents and the Agent SDK (not Claude Code, not extra usage in the apps). Credits expire monthly, need a linked Console organization, require no payment method, and when exhausted requests simply stop, so there is a hard cap and no surprise bill. This is API-key authentication, which the legal page names as the supported route for developers building products, and it still lets a Claude agent with tools (Agent SDK) run on a server, but it is not interactive Claude Code and it is metered at API rates against a small allowance. It may satisfy the preference to avoid open-ended pay-per-token billing while remaining clearly within terms.

setup_steps: 0. Resolve the terms question first: before building, ask Anthropic (sales or support, in writing) whether an unattended Claude Code session on a VPS, triggered by your CRM and sending messages to your own prospects, is permitted on your intended plan. The legal page invites this question. Consider a Team plan (Commercial Terms, admin controls) rather than personal Pro/Max for a company workload, and note that on Team an Owner must enable Channels, Remote Control and Routines toggles.

1. Provision a Linux VPS (Ubuntu 24.04 class, at least 4 GB RAM, 2 GB swap; community minimum is 2 GB but crashes were reported on low memory). Create a non-root user (for example agent), run loginctl enable-linger agent, deny all inbound except SSH (or use a private network such as Tailscale), install tmux, Node and Bun (channel plugins are Bun scripts), then install Claude Code with Anthropic's installer.

2. Authenticate with claude auth login over SSH (open the printed URL on your laptop, paste the code back). Choose setup-token only if you accept that claude.ai-hosted connectors and Remote Control will not work with it; in that case register Apify and other MCP servers locally with claude mcp add. Use a dedicated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for the agent and never run parallel -p jobs under the same credentials.

3. Create the agent project directory with: a short CLAUDE.md of stable rules; .claude/skills/ playbooks (discovery, enrichment, pitch, reply handling); .claude/settings.json with explicit allow rules and deny rules plus PreToolUse hooks that block anything outside the CRM tools; and .mcp.json pointing at a local stdio MCP server that wraps the Flask CRM API (narrow tools only: claim_task, get_conversation, draft_reply, request_approval, log_decision, heartbeat). Do not give the unattended session raw production SSH keys.

4. Choose the permission posture: preferred is dontAsk mode with allow rules for exactly the CRM MCP tools and the channel reply tool (anything else is denied instead of hanging) or auto mode with the classifier; use relay for ad-hoc approvals. Avoid dangerously-skip-permissions unless the whole session runs inside a container or VM as non-root. Run once interactively in tmux to pre-accept folder trust, MCP approval, and theme dialogs.

5. Event path: Flask receives the BSP webhook, writes the inbound message to the database (durable queue, source of truth), then POSTs only an event id and type (not the raw prospect text) to the local channel server on 127.0.0.1. The channel server is a custom MCP channel (webhook-receiver pattern from the channels reference), launched with the development-channels flag; the agent fetches the conversation through the CRM MCP tool so inbound text arrives as data, not as instructions. Optionally add the official Telegram or Discord channel with an owner-only allowlist for approvals and alerts.

6. Supervisor: write agent-supervisor.sh that ensures a tmux session (for example sales) is running claude with DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, the chosen permission mode and the channel flags, and that auto-answers only the known launch confirmation (development-channel warning) by matching its text. Run it from a systemd service with Restart=always and RestartSec=10 (ExecStart pointing at the foreground supervisor, not at tmux new-session -d). Pin the Claude Code version; update only after a test window.

7. Watchdog (systemd timer, about every 30s): liveness, readiness within 60s of spawn, canary ping via the heartbeat tool every 5-10 minutes, capture-pane scan for permission or needs-input dialogs, login-status check, RSS/CPU/zombie/disk thresholds, and a scheduled recycle when idle (every 2-6 hours, with --continue or a fresh session that rebuilds state from the CRM). Escalation ladder: Escape+Enter nudge, restart, then WhatsApp or Telegram alert to the owner. Add an outside dead-man ping so a dead VPS also alerts.

8. Scheduled jobs: for daily discovery, enrichment, pitch and page generation either (a) have cron on the VPS enqueue tasks in the CRM that the single resident session claims, so one login and one session do all work, or (b) use Routines for cloud-side jobs (1 hour minimum interval, claude.ai login required, connectors attach per routine). Do not rely on /loop for durable scheduling (7-day expiry, session-scoped).

9. Human control: put send approval in the CRM (the send tool refuses without an approved record), cap sends per day and per lead, route every uncertain case to a needs-human queue, wire the Notification hook and StopFailure hook to the owner alert channel, and schedule a daily digest. Build and test the kill switch layers (CRM agent_enabled flag, systemctl stop plus tmux kill-session, webhook disable, token revoke) before go-live.

10. Roll out in stages: two weeks draft-only (agent proposes, human sends), then supervised sending with low caps, reviewing the first runs closely, then raise limits. Review weekly: login health, usage against caps, watchdog incidents, Claude Code release notes and the Help Center page on Agent SDK and claude -p billing (it has changed repeatedly).

11. Keep a degraded-mode fallback that does not depend on the agent: Flask alerts a human if an inbound reply is unacknowledged for N minutes, and optionally keep an API-key path (for example the included monthly Max/Team API credits with the Agent SDK) ready for the case where the subscription login is blocked, expired, or your account is actioned.
limits_and_risks: Account risk: Anthropic can suspend or terminate access without notice and says it may enforce its authentication restrictions without notice. Suspension reasons are not disclosed and several users report unexplained suspensions and a poor appeal path. A single account also is a single point of failure for the sales operation, and Claude chat, Claude Code and Cowork on that account would be lost together.

Terms ambiguity: unattended automation by cron, webhook or chat bridge, and business use on Pro/Max, are not explicitly permitted by any source I found. The legal page says plan limits assume ordinary individual use and that developers building products or services should use API keys. Customer-facing autonomy increases the chance of being read as running a service.

Policy volatility: subscription coverage of third-party tools, claude -p and the Agent SDK changed in Jan, Feb, Apr, May, Jun and Oct 2026. The headless docs also say bare mode, which does not use subscription login, will become the default for claude -p in a future release (my inference: claude -p on a subscription login could stop working or be billed differently without further notice).

Preview status: Channels, Routines, Remote Control, agent view and the /fire endpoint are research previews; flags and protocol may change, flags are hidden from claude --help, and the allowlist blocks custom channels without a development flag that needs an interactive confirmation on each launch.

Stability: documented open bugs include channel sessions that stop reacting to inbound messages, a channel regression in 2.1.283, Telegram poller eviction by a second session, leaked plugin processes, and long-session memory/CPU runaway (3-17h on macOS reports). Many reports were closed as not planned by a stale-bot with no maintainer reply; Linux-specific long-run data is thin.

Auth: headless OAuth refresh has multiple unresolved or unacknowledged reports (Cloudflare 403/429 on refresh from VPS, -p not refreshing, concurrent jobs invalidating a shared credential). setup-token cannot do Remote Control or claude.ai connectors. Expect occasional manual re-login; an expired login halts an unattended session silently until someone acts.

Usage caps: 5-hour and weekly limits are shared with all other use on the account, auto-continue does not cover Remote Control, background sessions, -p, or resets more than 24 hours away, and a heavy autonomous day can exhaust the week. Routines add separate hourly caps.

Security: the agent combines shell, connectors, CRM access and outbound messaging while reading untrusted prospect text. Without architectural separation (data not instructions, narrow tools, server-side approvals, no shell for the reply-handling session) a prompt injection can cause unwanted sends or data leakage. Permission relay approval authority extends to anyone on the allowlist.
Message loss: events are dropped silently if the session is down or the channel is not loaded; platform-side retention (Telegram) is not a reliable queue. The CRM must hold the queue.

Evidence quality: no independent multi-month production case study found; most setup guides are vendor or hobbyist blogs, several sell hosting. Reddit content was not accessible to the search tool, so Reddit-only anecdotes are missing. Ban statistics circulating in blogs could not be verified and were excluded.
WhatsApp-side risk: unofficial WhatsApp Web (Baileys) channel plugins carry WhatsApp account-restriction risk; use the official BSP path already in place.
result.verdict: PARTLY. A subscription-powered, always-on Claude Code operator is realistic for a small business as a supervised, best-effort component, not as an unattended system you can leave alone. It works because Anthropic's own binary can run in tmux on a VPS, Channels/Remote Control/background sessions/Routines are documented building blocks, and practitioners run variants of it. It is not safe to treat as production-grade because (1) several building blocks are research previews with open, unacknowledged reliability bugs (deaf channels, auth refresh, long-session runaway); (2) unattended business use on a Pro/Max login is not explicitly permitted and the rules have shifted repeatedly, with account action possible without notice; and (3) usage caps and re-login needs can silently stop it. The minimum reliable setup is: official binary only (no token extraction, no third-party harness on the subscription); one resident session in tmux under a foreground supervisor with systemd; the CRM database as source of truth with a durable inbound queue and human fallback if the agent does not acknowledge within minutes; a layered watchdog including an end-to-end canary, login and usage alerts, and scheduled recycling; narrow server-enforced tools, approvals and kill switches outside the model; untrusted prospect text treated strictly as data; pinned Claude Code version; and a documented degraded mode. Before investing, get written confirmation from Anthropic for this exact use and consider a Team plan, or keep the included Max/Team API credits with the Agent SDK as the clearly in-terms fallback.
open_questions: Will Anthropic confirm in writing that an unattended Claude Code session on a VPS, fed by a CRM webhook and messaging the company's own prospects, is permitted on Team (Commercial Terms) or on Max (Consumer Terms)? Is Team the required plan for business use?
Which plan do you intend to use (Pro, Max 5x/20x, Team), and does your organisation have an Owner who can enable Channels, Remote Control and Routines?
Is the intended host the Linux VPS only, or also this Windows Server desktop? Linux with tmux has the most community evidence; Windows evidence is thin.
Will the headless-default --bare change for claude -p land, and will subscription login remain supported for non-interactive runs? No official statement either way.
How much unattended autonomy is acceptable for outbound WhatsApp (draft-only, approved-template-only, or free text) and what are the daily caps and legal constraints (BSP template rules, opt-in)?
What is the expected inbound volume and required latency? Per-reply wake-ups consume subscription quota quickly, so a high-volume inbox may exceed caps.

Does the current Claude Code release (about 2.1.299) still show the channel-goes-deaf and poller-eviction behaviours on Linux? Needs a read-only soak test before any commitment; I did not install or run anything.
Do you want the CRM MCP server and watchdog designed and reviewed as a separate task (including the prompt-injection boundary between inbound prospect text and tools that can send or spend)?
